### Customer and grant engineer operating course

1. **Select the original customer workshare.** Open Installations and create or reopen the original environmental source preparation. Load the complete selection with every selected original packet and its supporting file. Select the appropriate installed profile while retaining the original case, canonical plan, phase dependencies, scope, milestones, correction terms and schedule. Review the actual source population, authorized access and receiving application with the customer.
2. **Prepare the whole supplier input.** In **Prepare original source workshares**, review each phase’s effort pointer, unit and full total, then choose **Prepare complete native package**. The unchanged source preparer checks the entire selected files and original plan before producing the complete supplier documents, receiving material and source-preparation record. The private complete executable source package and operator quickstart retain the source-only command and every input needed to prepare this same selection.
3. **Bind the accountable operating roles.** Through the original case writer, attach the complete cohort and inspect the native preview. For each workshare, select the actual merchant/source owner, commissioning payer, independent buyer, scientific reviewer, receiving engineer and acceptance owner; declare their host/runtime, source authorization and approved useful-task spending. Open the complete Installation draft, review its pending choices and save in the existing case. Customer dates and delivery clocks follow the original agreement and required source/access readiness.
4. **Operate the complete selected product.** Laboratory receiving retains the original five-slot contract and seals every selected upload, native current/baseline families, saved editors and exact job/result identity. Geotech’s original workbook and separately bound reissue remain together. Water Quality scientific mode retains both complete source editions and seven output formats; KiWIS commissioning retains the saved source/time/quality decisions and all eight outputs. The operator resumes an interrupted upload, job or receiving operation through its original request and retained state.
5. **Receive the working result and return corrections.** Export the complete case with its source, reviews, original outcomes and Installation edition. The receiving engineer imports it into an independent workspace, reopens the selected edition, operates the agreed customer application and retains the complete result. Record actual observations and explicitly review any returned changes before saving the following Installation edition. The source and authorisation for earlier outputs stay attached to their original work.
6. **Record acceptance and the next useful task.** The customer’s actual accepted output, receiving person, corrections and handover determine its milestone. Enter actual production effort under its selected commercial or funded assignment once. A later laboratory reissue or reporting window begins another expressly selected useful task; reopening or replaying the acquired result continues the earlier one.

Both the original [JavaScript launcher](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/6d18ad532aef87aad8982da1ff3c3426655ae014/stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace/launch.mjs) and [managed Python launcher](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/6d18ad532aef87aad8982da1ff3c3426655ae014/stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace/managed_launch.py) include the same four profiles and full guide in their selected source. The managed and direct installations therefore expose the same catalogue and operating contract.

## Report and content commissioning and complete receiving

**Recurring report and content handover.** The [Superset report workspace](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4042d88f2fec313cfde80fff8df05aceaf5708f2/products/superset-report/OPERATING.md) and [Directus collection workspace](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/6bf48482bcde72e03698df3b6bd63cf584ce64df/products/directus-content-data/OPERATING.md) support a concrete recurring customer task: deliver a selected operational report or content catalogue, review its next useful edition and transfer the working service to another maintainer. The commissioning workorder identifies the source owner, merchant, implementation payer, independent buyer and receiving engineer; their authorized saved report or collection; the complete output and destination; its freshness trigger; and the separately advertised paid requests needed to finish it. The operator agrees the baseline output and later reporting period, approved query or content change before assigning the remaining installation work. Both applications use the original dataset, merchant, buyer and receiving engines.

The operator and receiving engineer carry the same installation through five connected stages:

1. **Install the complete selected application.** Select the original [Superset package recipe](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4042d88f2fec313cfde80fff8df05aceaf5708f2/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/selections/superset-report.json) or [Directus package recipe](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/6bf48482bcde72e03698df3b6bd63cf584ce64df/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/selections/directus-content-data.json) from its immutable source revision. Retain the original package, source manifest, runtime profile and installation record, then open **Superset chart data** or **Directus collection data** in managed Applications. The Superset native programme selects the maintained native, schema and operator features with Stellar SDK 16.3.1, an explicit supported version within the original `^16.3.0` requirement. The original installer checks the archive and complete source before loading the selected dependencies. Provider credentials remain references supplied by the receiving host.
2. **Approve the exact source and its next edition.** Superset retains the authenticated account, saved chart/query context, all returned query responses, native limits, filters, resolved reporting period and original numeric values; the operator explicitly chooses the query to publish. A returned row count describes that query result. Directus retains the authenticated account, collection, field/relation definitions, selected query, all observed item pages and native change readback. Missing, null and empty values keep their distinct meanings. Compare the baseline and successor on the selected keys and population, review the changes and distribution rights, then publish through the original merchant. Its native version writer retains both generations and the selected revision.
3. **Complete the original buyer acquisition.** Review the advertised resource, selected payment option and aggregate task budget. Acquire every agreed page or file and receive the complete dataset and source material in CSV, JSONL or SQLite as required by the customer. If publication advances while acquisition is in progress, the buyer continues its original selected snapshot. Reopening an interrupted operation uses its retained page, attempt and delivery history; completion requires the agreed output, including genuine zero, empty and unchanged values.
4. **Receive and continue the whole working project.** Export the original source, reviews, publisher generations, prepared buyer configurations, acquired sessions and delivered files. A second engineer supplies destination runtime references, restores the original publisher and acquisition, delivers saved output and selects a later publisher generation. Export that progressed project for another receiver, then reopen the same original incoming handover at the first destination. The first receiver's later publisher choice and acquired history remain intact. Managed Stop/reopen and a cold application restart return to the same operating state.
5. **Accept the useful result in the original operating case.** In [Delivery operations → Cohort acceptance](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/fcea2b04a19d9c14bbd337124ecdc83f5e36425c/stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace/OPERATIONS-COHORT.md), associate the named deployments, original approved task, selected source/snapshot, complete accepted output and receiving engineer. For a paid operation, join each distinct native transfer to its actual facilitator, approved intent and delivered output, retaining the original attempt/completion clocks. A later useful purchase has a new approved intent; reopening, replaying or transferring an acquired result continues its original purchase.

Both complete provider applications and their selected-package recipes are merged, including portable original buyer sessions and received publisher history. The [Superset native programme](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/7cde1c2537e038b43388f7286fd9c88a0d12994a/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/superset/examples/README.md) uses the retained original Census workbooks to exercise authenticated Superset 6.1, asynchronous query completion, a sixteen-row acquisition, successor publication, full-project receiving and continued use. Its selected-runtime receiver uses the [maintained source installer](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/7cde1c2537e038b43388f7286fd9c88a0d12994a/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install.mjs); the complete original source bodies are recovered and native runtime acquisition/build continues under the same operation. ## Groundwater scenario modelling and receiving

A groundwater modelling team needs the complete selected model, the basis for each scenario change and an inspectable result that another engineer can reopen. Aquaveo’s published [Tethys services](https://aquaveo.com/services/tethys) and [MODFLOW support in GMS](https://aquaveo.com/software/gms/models-utilities/modflow) provide a specific prospective commissioning fit. ## Service recovery that reaches the buyer’s books

### The customer outcome

A buyer needs the useful service it purchased and a correct record of what happened when delivery failed. The merchant may recover the output, agree a partial return or identify a remaining correction. The buyer then needs the credit to reach the right expense item, reporting period and accountant handoff. Keeping those links saves staff from repeatedly matching support tickets, payment records, exported files and bookkeeping rows.

The Service-to-buyer operation carries that work through one saved customer case. The merchant selects its Service report and explicit monetary basis. Its configured accounting operator reviews the adjustment and the returned-transfer evidence. The buyer receives the complete capture, codes the original purchase and credit, resolves period issues and issues the period. The accountant’s reviewed return comes back to those original rows. A receiving engineer can reopen the continued project with its source, decisions and customer files.

### Architecture and operator control

The existing merchant workspace owns the Service terms, report, proposal, prepared intent and native outcome. The configured accounting workspace verifies the selected payment and adjustment and exports the original purchase, linked credit and complete adjustment statuses. Buyer Expenses owns source intake, exact native-unit allocations, issue dispositions and issued periods. The Accountant workspace owns its handoff and permitted returned fields.

Each step uses the configured owner’s existing workspace and request journal. Before dispatch, the operator reviews the exact input and original workspace selection. When a response is interrupted, recovery reuses the retained request and body; an already committed result is returned before applying a current-version check. Appending the outcome preserves other operators’ intervening case work. The complete export carries the applications, buyer state, issued period, accountant files and original requests together.

The monetary decision stays explicit: the Service report supplies the observed event and reviewed basis; the responsible operator authorizes the adjustment. The original purchase, adjustment status, returned-transfer proof and buyer coding remain separately inspectable throughout receiving.

The [complete installed operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/6f976ed642b580f362c0748fd78137e81a85cf18/products/pmtiles-operations/OPERATING.md) connects source selection, dependency installation, map authoring, merchant publication, customer receiving and original accounting.

**The useful operator task.** Staff retain the original regional archive, its matching style and required attribution. Native inspection checks the archive and source/style relationships. Staff save an edition, review its complete files against the current release, publish it, and serve the selected map through the original PMTiles/Martin runtime. Later work retains earlier editions and the release chain. The authoring application can stop and reopen on its saved browser origin while retaining the operator's draft. Restoration follows the published release's actual predecessor.

The complete customer package carries the frozen database, retained source objects, editions, reviews, releases, attribution, source code and selected map runtime. Receiving verifies that package and rebinds its original runtime paths on the customer's host; the customer reopens the same workspace and can restore earlier releases. The original Object Buyer supplies paid/private-object acquisition: its recorded ObjectDelivery binds the complete received object to the archive adopted by the map workspace. Its complete customer backup carries the original payment, response and assembled-file state.

**Selling a complete map or operating package.** The merchant selects the original retained output, fixes its complete byte identity and chunk plan, prepares its advertised price and complete-download cost, and stages the offer through the existing SF30/SF82 release workflow. The buyer approves that exact object and aggregate budget, continues the original SF88 requests and assembles every agreed byte. It can then adopt the purchased map into the existing workspace or receive the complete operations package. A lost response reopens the same release, request, retained response and receiving target.

The industrial browser operator joins offer authoring, reviewed seller activation and owned Stop, customer purchase/adoption/receiving and accounting recovery on the original map page. Retained drafts and pending requests stay bound to their workspace, merchant alias and browser origin. The same 21 commerce tools are available through merchant MCP and the installed CLI. Accounting reads the retained native command before continuing its original range and completes a checkpoint only after the range and outcomes have completed. Managed Applications, browser and MCP operate the same saved merchant and customer records.

**Commissioning and customer responsibilities.** The original Camptocamp workshare proposes **USD 9,600 for 72 planned hours over fifteen business days**. It provides a concrete commercial installation scope around this existing map-release product. The commissioning work selects the actual customer archives and styles, rights and attribution, host, receiving engineer, operational responsibilities and accepted handover. The customer's original case retains the selected commercial terms and correspondence.

The original first contact was sent to Camptocamp on **12 October 2026 at 17:25:21 UTC**. The same company operation retains the complete proposed workshare, verified original sent message and correspondence history. The complete Case Receiving package imports that workshare, starts its five-phase delivery board and reopens its original exports through the existing company application.

**Application to the existing funded work.** If a map installation is selected for the grant cohort, its workorder names the merchant, independent buyer and commissioning payer; the approved source and release; the useful complete output; the priced operation; and the receiving application. A changed regional source, reviewed map edition or new customer task can supply a useful later purchase. T1 applies the existing source, buyer authority and handover components to those selected systems. T2 takes that same operation through both independently operated facilitators and the deployed recovery cases. T3 covers mainnet use, later useful purchases and independent production recovery and handover. This uses the application's existing six funded packages and **400-hour / USD 38,000 / 150-day** plan, with the completed reusable source accounted for before the prospective installation estimate.

The standalone product and operating selection are delivered through the original SCF thread. The current paid-output source and complete installed guide above include the reviewed source/archive, release, purchase, accounting and browser recovery joins. The full producer, map browser, cold customer, MCP, managed Applications and paid-browser receiving remains assigned to the original Muse operation, `CAMPT0CAMP-PMTILES-RELEASE-OPERATIONS-20261012`, with its selected READY installation and actual approved signer/policy allocation. Its native result and retained customer files will establish the completed receiving outcome.

## Merchant settlement, customer billing and accountant receiving

A working Stellar merchant needs the useful paid result and a financial record its customer and accountant can continue. The maintained product joins original settlement accounting, customer invoicing and credit review, dated receipt allocation, credit notes and refunds, bank source matching, installment schedules, service closing and Xero document receiving around the same accounting workspace. The customer can follow the charge, actual money, remaining obligation and ongoing service through one complete operating history.

### The customer's complete operating task

The merchant's resource receipts and an implementation or service invoice retain their own original records. A paid resource begins with the approved HTTP or MCP intent, selected payment terms, native settlement and complete output. A prepaid allowance continues its original acquired order while later requests consume service units. A separately agreed customer invoice begins with the accepted scope and a reviewed issued document. Its selected Stellar wallet request retains both the invoice-currency value and exact native or issued-asset amount; receiving binds the verified transfer to the same customer obligation. Its receipt allocations and credits determine the dated amount due; a payment plan places that existing amount on agreed collection dates.

The accounting reconciliation retains the actual network, asset, transaction identity and atomic amount. Commercial-currency amounts retain the merchant's explicit valuation and accounting basis. The customer, accountant and receiving engineer can follow the resulting source link without converting an installment, repeated export or imported document status into another purchase.

|Operating stage|Customer and operator result|Original record carried forward|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|Agree the source or service|Name the useful request and complete output, or select the accepted implementation/service quotation.|Buyer intent and terms, or original quotation, customer response and accounting customer.|
|Complete and reconcile the Stellar operation|Receive the full result and review the original settlement, independent network verification and delivery.|Native event, network/asset/atomic units, transaction fingerprint, complete result and selected accounting source.|
|Issue and receive customer charges|Review exact invoice amounts, dates and billing identity; record the actual receipt and its effective invoice allocations.|Frozen invoice files, receipt identity, allocation dates and explicit valuation where selected.|
|Continue collections and corrections|Review credits, dated releases, agreed installment editions and the customer's complete statement.|Original invoice/receipt history, schedule basis and every retained customer edition.|
|Receive into the accountant's organisation|Map issued invoices and credits to actual Xero templates, contact names, accounts and tax fields; receive its original returned document results.|Mapping version, immutable package, external document IDs, exact amounts, validation and correction history.|
|Hand over the running operation|Receive the complete saved workspace and its operating sources, reopen it and continue the customer's agreed task.|Original accounting journal, customer files, request identities, encrypted backup and post-backup reconciliation.|

### Original bank statements, customer remittances and retained account closes

The [complete bank product](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/933219ca2f66ebbaf28d5a7ef69cefe278de2a98/products/merchant-bank-statements/README.md) extends the same merchant accounting workspace into daily cash reconciliation. The operator receives the original OFX, QFX, explicitly mapped CSV or CAMT.053 XML statement, selects its actual account and currency section, and retains the entire source file and interpretation. Existing customer, invoice, receipt and accounting workspace identities continue through that intake.

### Receive the bank's original CAMT.053 statement

The maintained adapter accepts the exact camt.053.001.02 and camt.053.001.08 namespaces. The operator can select the source version or let the reader identify the original namespace. The [complete CAMT.053 operator and source guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/933219ca2f66ebbaf28d5a7ef69cefe278de2a98/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/receivables/bank-statements/CAMT053.md) explains the supported structures, account selection, original transaction detail and closing rules.

One original statement entry remains one cash movement. Its original amount is an exact decimal string; the current credit/debit indicator supplies its direction. A reversal indicator remains visible alongside that direction. Nested batch and transaction-detail amounts describe the entry and retain their own identifiers, parties, remittance information, charges, return details and currency information. They remain subordinate to the original entry's cash amount.

Account identity retains its original IBAN or other identifier, scheme, issuer and servicing institution. The source reader keeps the bank's references, entry and detail ordering, booking and value dates, source positions and original XML. Namespace and version checks apply to the supported source structure. Version .08 supplementary content retains the original opaque envelope, so the operator can inspect the complete supplied content in the source.

The review separates booked entries, pending observations, information-only entries and unresolved status values. The full statement report keeps each original observation and its reason for treatment. The ordinary account preview retains the compact metadata used by the browser and SDK; the original file and complete parsed report remain available for subsequent review. An unchanged file and interpretation reuses its saved import. Another file with the same original reference and agreeing financial fields retains a copy linked to the existing cash movement. Changed financial fields, including credit/debit direction or reversal, enter source-conflict review.

The neutral bank screen presents statement and account metadata, source-period and pagination information, original balance controls, and every original entry. Entry-detail pages retain all nested transaction details with their original order. The same [source API and versioned type contract](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/933219ca2f66ebbaf28d5a7ef69cefe278de2a98/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/receivables/bank-statements/source.d.ts) serves the source reader, account preview and existing bank writer. The [installed command preparation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/933219ca2f66ebbaf28d5a7ef69cefe278de2a98/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/receivables/bank-statements/cli.mjs) reads an original regular file's exact bytes and writes the private JSON request used by the established preview/import flow; its explicit format, version and detail-policy options reproduce the browser's source choice. The [complete source-format guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/933219ca2f66ebbaf28d5a7ef69cefe278de2a98/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/receivables/bank-statements/SOURCE_FORMATS.md) connects this workflow to the existing OFX/QFX/CSV interfaces.

### Receive a complete statement across original pages

A merchant's daily CAMT statement can span several original XML files or several statement sections in one file. The [complete page workflow](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/091b359d793684764f4da19af1bb563d05aa45b0/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/receivables/bank-statements/PAGE_ASSEMBLY.md), delivered in [PR1185](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/1185) and the [complete product handover](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/1209), connects those originals to the same account close. The operator receives each page into its saved account, selects the complete statement, reviews its original period, grouping and page sequence, then uses the assembled original balances in the existing close.

Each selected page retains its source file, selected statement section, original references, summary and booked balance boundaries. The assembler requires exactly one through the final page, compatible account/currency and original period, connected intermediate boundaries and a final booked closing balance. A common original sequence establishes the grouping when supplied; the operator retains an explicit account-period explanation when the source lacks that common identity. The bank's summary scope remains a reviewed choice. Each original booked entry must still resolve to exactly one current posted cash transaction. Every current posted movement in that account period must also be covered by the complete selected source; offsetting extra transactions still require review.

This lets an accountant follow the full statement from the first original opening through every page to the final closing. The browser shows those controls and source issues; the typed client and installed CLI receive the same selection. The saved close carries every source import, the complete page review, exact transaction/posting exports, editable account data, participating customer records and all original XML files. An empty page still belongs to the retained statement. Source corrections retain the earlier close and its complete original archive.

The actual assembler and existing close-review domain received the published SWIFT numeric worked example as explicit review input: seven entries across two pages, opening 100.00, intermediate 110.00 and final closing 138.00. The resulting close review is ready with zero difference. Missing pages, inconsistent original sequence, reversed balance timestamps and missing or duplicated current cash bindings enter source review. The installed [original-workspace receiving course](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/c15e2ea80154078886011d792e0aa7be6a5a94b2/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/receivables/bank-statements/PAGE_ASSEMBLY_RECEIVE.mjs) continues the existing bank operation through the real writer, full account export, saved-request recovery and cold reopening.

The [accountant workbench](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/c15e2ea80154078886011d792e0aa7be6a5a94b2/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/receivables/bank-statements/accountant-receiving/ACCOUNTANT_RECEIVING.md), merged in PR1149, opens the complete original account archive. ### Match the original cash and retain the customer's obligation

Bank reconciliation and the original Bank receipts desk share customer receipt identities and exact source coverage. A 97.00 bank credit can match a 100.00 original customer receipt and a separate -3.00 fee while the invoice retains its 100.00 allocation. A payment covering several source credits keeps each covered portion; correcting one portion retains the other customer cash and original allocation lineage. Original refunds remain separate negative movements. Every posting conserves the source's exact signed amount and selected currency precision.

The same service receives a customer's original remittance CSV through the [complete remittance desk and source format](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4d8349987383312683eb554228f9122649233891/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/receivables/REMITTANCES.md). It matches saved customer references and issued invoice numbers, reviews exact payment and allocation dates, and reuses an agreeing existing receipt with its original bank or Stellar source. The operator saves the reviewed request and receives the entire conflict-free batch through the original accounting writer. Reopening retains the original source, review, payment IDs and allocation history.

The [native remittance workflow](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4d8349987383312683eb554228f9122649233891/stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/ACCOUNTING_REMITTANCES.md) exposes the same original controller through the merchant MCP owner, typed customer client and durable accounting CLI. Complete inline CSV or a configured source alias is retained in the preview; the original workspace identity, ledger revision, source bytes and full review digest bind the prepared request. The saved operation directory carries that exact request through execution and response recovery. Each retained batch provides its original source.csv, review.json, review.csv, batch.json and manifest.json through the existing paged file reader. The accounting backup carries the same batch and source bytes.

A matching Stellar receipt keeps its original network, atomic asset amount, asset identity, transaction fingerprint, transfer evidence and recorded commercial valuation. Allocation uses that recorded commercial currency and precision. Dated invoice balances and the receipt's effective accounting date, later allocations, refunds and reservations constrain the complete proposed batch. Exact repeated instructions recover their existing results; an identical active allocation in another download identifies the original allocation for review. Corrections retain the existing dated release and allocation history.

The complete browser/HTTP arm merged in PR612 and the native operator arm in PR706. Execution of the actual original planner/controller, native owner/client and request writer with an in-memory workspace adapter received a 324-byte BOM/CRLF CSV: USD100.00 split into USD40.00 and USD60.00, leaving both invoices paid with one receipt, two allocations and one batch. Original-request recovery returned the same batch, replay added nothing and the source reopened byte-for-byte. Changed CSV and workspace identities were rejected by the native preview validator. The independently exercised planner also preserved dated refund reservations and failed-group rollback. This is a working foundation for the selected merchant's actual source mapping, independent operator receiving and complete accounting handover within the existing deployment packages.

A period close uses the original account, inclusive statement dates and reviewed balance basis. Its preview checks opening balance plus booked movements against the reported closing balance and presents unresolved source or matching work. CAMT source eligibility includes the original complete period, pagination, compatible opening/closing booked balances and unresolved report, statement or entry issues. Available and forward balances retain their original meanings. A usable source entry can be received while the source still requires resolution before a complete-period close.

A retained close contains complete transaction and posting CSVs, original statements, readable reconciliation, editable account JSON, participating customer account exports and the full file/TAR handover. Reopening an affected close and applying a reviewed replacement preserves its earlier downloadable edition.

[PR1149](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/1149) merged that complete sixteen-file product and its original Bank entry points. For a selected merchant installation, the commissioning workorder names the original account and period, statement formats, receiving accountant, permitted customer documents and intended review return. ### Customer service close, corrections and complete handover

A recurring-service merchant needs to explain the work performed after a prepaid pass was acquired. Customer statements now carries that whole operating task: maintain the customer and order assignment, retain the native service captures, choose each pass's service period, review the statement, issue the saved cycle and give the customer its complete files. The installed [customer closing workbench](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/de02bd1d960df2cc462d62c1c71f75fee5e95dee/stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/ACCOUNTING_STATEMENT_WORKBENCH.md) and [service-close planner](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/de02bd1d960df2cc462d62c1c71f75fee5e95dee/stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/ACCOUNTING_STATEMENT_SERVICE_PLANNER.md) use the same merchant accounting workspace as the original purchase and service records.

The closing basis is a pair of actual captures for the same immutable pass. Their original capture times, plan revision and entitlement remain visible. The planner groups these sources by customer and pass and shows current, superseded and withdrawn statements, earlier customer assignments, gaps and ambiguous boundaries. Where history gives a single clear next opening and a later closing capture, it offers those sources for review. The operator chooses the exact boundaries and can add several periods for the same pass. Optional purchase-date filters remain separate from the service boundary.

|Operator stage|Decision made in the installed application|Complete result retained|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|Customers and service|Review the customer profile, original order assignment and configured native capture imports.|Customer versions, assignment history, exact capture sources and saved requests.|
|Plan service close|Choose customers, passes, opening and closing captures, the completed accounting run and any original statement being corrected.|Explicit source selections, period and lifecycle context, with the current native source identities.|
|Review the plan|Open the full native usage preview and review every selected customer period.|Complete portable plan JSON, readable HTML and CSV; importing that plan restores its actual selections.|
|Prepare the original cycle|Save the customer reviews before issuing the statements.|Frozen native reviews, the saved preparation request and one durable cycle containing all selected rows.|
|Issue and resume|Issue the reviewed rows and continue an interrupted cycle from its saved requests.|Original statement numbers, per-customer progress and complete delivered files as each row finishes.|
|Correct or withdraw|Review a replacement against the original retained statement, or record the withdrawal reason.|Linked statement editions, original files and the current lifecycle history.|
|Customer handover|Group the customer's passes and periods and download its complete available packet.|A readable index, statement and period registers, complete original statement files and saved status snapshots.|
|Independent continuation|Reopen the customer packet or restore the complete private operator cycle.|Usable relative links and original files for the customer; saved reviews and requests for the receiving operator.|


The customer packet keeps each statement and period readable as its own record. A partially completed cycle still produces a useful register of the available statements and the rows awaiting completion. When a correction or withdrawal is recorded later, the operator refreshes the original delivered statements and prepares the updated customer packet. Repeating an export of unchanged files reuses its retained snapshot; earlier packets preserve the state they contained at delivery. The complete cycle archive carries the operator's saved work for a restart or handover.

The service statement retains the original purchase amounts and measured allowance activity in their own fields. A separately issued invoice, native payment receipt or agreed installment continues through its existing financial record. Customer closing makes those continuing service records inspectable alongside the useful paid output, while the original purchase register supplies its network, transaction and atomic amount.

For a recurring-service operator, the result is a repeatable close: identify the customer and purchased service, explain the activity since the previous close, deliver the statement, and preserve the records needed to answer a later question or correct the period. Staff can continue an interrupted close from its saved cycle and prepare a complete customer handover from the statements already delivered.

For a commissioned customer, the workorder identifies the actual merchant workspace and native capture sources, customer/order mapping, intended service cadence, receiving staff and complete customer output. The existing merchant-resource package covers the selected source and identity adaptation; authority and handover covers the next operator and correction workflow; production recovery covers the complete state and customer-file restoration. This makes continuing customer service a concrete operating outcome within the existing six-package implementation.

Download the complete operator archive, recover the same saved request, and reopen the account and response from the existing full backup. The resulting account and collection records provide the presenter's concrete customer explanation.

## Wholesale order commissioning and complete ERP receiving

A wholesaler needs a supplier or customer feed to become the intended ERP order, with the original attachments, exact quantities and prices, and a way to reconcile partial processing or later corrections. Its source is merged in private Commons PR35577, at `35ae501bdc454284637c46725ba47c2293e374dd`; the original company workorder and delivery retain its commercial owner and source custody. This is an implementation candidate; the original contact form has not been submitted and no company email has been sent.

**One complete operating task.** An operator imports the complete feed and attachments, reviews exact-number mappings and the selected source edition, prepares order candidates, and explicitly authorizes processing against the selected target. Read-only allocation and order reconciliation then preserves what the native target actually returned. Attributed corrections create later reviewed editions; reversal coverage retains the affected original work. The browser and CLI expose the same operating history, reports, folder delivery, full backup/restore, and case-handoff export. Original source, requested processing, observed target state and receiving acknowledgment remain separately inspectable.

**Observed result and remaining commissioning.** All 44 complete source files, totaling 464,818 bytes, were read back after merge. Actual local Python/Node, HTTP, installed-build, source-to-report, folder-delivery, two-backup, restore and reopen checks passed. There were **zero Metasfresh target calls**: no customer feed, target or credentials was supplied. The target tenant, original business input, responsible reviewer and receiving engineer are selected in the commissioning agreement before native target acceptance. Source and customer packages remain private; this application describes their capabilities and operating evidence without redistributing those files or treating them as a new public Stellar release.

**The proposed workshare.** The original prepared offer is **USD 12,600 for 96 hours over 15 active business days**: USD 3,150 for agreed scope/start, USD 6,300 for accepted native commissioning, and USD 3,150 for complete receiving. It remains a proposed offer with its original company owner; customer agreement, start, invoices and collections are unset. Its complete local product supplies the foundation for the customer's actual feed mapping, target configuration, reviewed processing, corrections and receiving procedure.

**Effort and cash remain tied to that workorder.** At the application's USD 95/hour assumption, 96 hours allocates **USD 9,120 to labor and leaves USD 3,480 before other costs**. A 25% effort increase gives 120 hours / USD 11,400, leaving USD 1,200 before other costs; labor-only break-even is approximately 132.63 hours. The first USD 3,150 installment would cover approximately 33.16 modeled hours only if actually collected. These are planning comparisons, not incurred cost or received cash. This proposal is separate from the original agency/provider groups, the groundwater proposal and the existing dated portfolio scenarios. Actual source repair, correction, customer waiting and receiving effort inform its agreed schedule and final delivery cost.

**Future Stellar installation in the existing six packages.** A funded selection would name the commissioning payer, authorized ERP/source owner, resource merchant, independent buyer and receiving engineer. It would select a specific publishable order/allocation report or agreed service result, its private versus delivered files, customer purpose and later-use trigger. The existing merchant HTTP or MCP path would then bind that resource to its reviewed network, asset, atomic price and original buyer request. T1 covers the selected source/runtime and consumer mapping plus authority and handover; T2 covers two-facilitator use and recovery of the original paid operation; T3 covers production rollout, recurring useful results and independent restore/support. That is future customer-specific Stellar engineering within the existing six packages. The private generic ERP implementation is not billed again to the grant, and this proposed workshare adds no purchase, independent merchant/buyer, mainnet deployment or collected revenue to the existing totals.

## Public Assistance portfolio commissioning and recurring review

Recovery programme analysts can commission a complete review of an agreed disaster cohort: retain original declarations, applicants and obligated projects; resolve source joins; assign follow-ups; and deliver a reviewed edition into the programme’s existing system. The workorder names the payer, merchant, independent buyer, receiving engineer, useful output and recurring purchase.

The [merged OpenFEMA exchange](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/a5eaac406a60502246e45cf003761340bcf355e2/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/openfema/DATA_INTEGRATION.md) receives the destination schema, retains its reviewed field mapping, exports every selected project, reconciles the complete customer CSV and imports selected analyst decisions into a new native version. Its browser, CLI, 41-tool merchant and typed client share the original workspace. The DR 4724 example contains **195 funded projects, 43 applicants and two declaration areas**. The full native run matched all 195 unchanged rows, applied one internal analyst decision with all four financial totals preserved, and reopened and restored the complete archive.

The October 12 DR 4935 source supplies an early-programme edition: **23 declaration areas, zero applicant rows and zero funded-project rows**. The exchange retains that starting edition and customer-only records awaiting source publication. The merchant prepares the accepted version and payment terms; the buyer receives the complete agreed output, source, mapping and review history.

For a selected installation, **T1** delivers the destination mapping, host, buyer integration and independent handover. **T2** deploys the useful operation through both selected facilitators and recovers interrupted payment or delivery. **T3** completes recurring mainnet use, release/rollback and receiving-host recovery. These customer-specific adaptations remain within the existing **$38,000 / 400-hour / 150-day**, two-merchant/two-buyer plan and its original usage targets.

## External buyer onboarding and study-operations commissioning

The actual Veridex invitation and MedStar technical-partner referral define two concrete implementation tasks. The first concerns an external Stellar buyer; the second concerns an adjacent study and reporting workflow. Their original proposed commercial terms, software capabilities and customer roles are set out below.

### Veridex: an external buyer's first complete operation

### The observed need

In the original October 11 conversation, Emmanuel explained that Veridex already has a conformance suite covering exact payments and settlement. He invited the existing SF88 buyer CLI into the testnet cohort to identify third-party findings and operator UX friction, with endpoint details to follow alignment. That is a concrete need for an external buyer to connect, understand the offered operation and recover a usable result. It is not a request to duplicate the provider's conformance suite.

Bryce's controlling follow-up at 15:23:17 UTC proposes **$1,500 fixed over five business days** for one mutually agreed Veridex `stellar:testnet` exact-payment route. It follows the earlier open-collaboration note and retains route-specific configuration, bounded SF88 adaptation, a reproducible original challenge/approval/response/settlement flow, onboarding/runbook and one agreed acceptance review. Delivery begins after agreed scope and acceptance criteria, received payment and endpoint/access availability. A reciprocal alternative needs written deliverables, usable benefits, timing and usage rights commensurate with the contribution. The latest original thread contains no returned endpoint, selected account or agreement.

The human invitation is therefore evidence of a specific external integration problem. The commercial terms remain a proposal. It supplies no independent customer purchase, paid implementation revenue or selected grant participant.

### The complete unit of work

|Part of the operation|Existing foundation|Work to finish for the agreed route|What the receiving operator uses|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|Connect and understand|SF88 retains the actual endpoint, operation, arguments and source/payment requirements.|Configure the returned route, actual supported network/asset/recipient, account and intended output; adapt only the selected buyer seam that differs.|The original route configuration and one documented useful request.|
|Approve and execute|The buyer keeps the challenge and reviewed terms before signing, and separates the original dispatch from its outcome.|Resolve the route's actual requirement and response handling in the existing buyer.|The original 402 challenge, visible approval and returned application response.|
|Inspect the result|The product retains complete returned bytes and the original payment/delivery record.|Map the route's complete output into the agreed buyer view or typed client without discarding source meaning.|A usable response with its native settlement record, rather than an isolated success indicator.|
|Continue and hand over|Original operations, received files and configuration can reopen through the same product.|Resolve the actual onboarding/UX findings found in this integration and document the selected route.|Reproducible setup, the operated request, findings and the proposed single acceptance review.|


This table describes the offered work, not a completed Veridex operation. The demonstration already available to a reviewer is the retained HPD paid-query operation. It proves the buyer's existing complete-result and receiving foundation. The Veridex route must have its own original endpoint, request, response and settlement before it can be reported as operated.

For the grant, this is a useful commissioning pattern for T1's customer adaptation and T2's same-service compatibility. The exact route, merchant, buyer, payer and receiving operator still come from the selected installation. Veridex's participation does not by itself select those roles or replace the requirement that the same useful service operate through both testnet facilitators.

**Original evidence:** business-account the original conversation; human invitation `1a12b7fe875fca98`, October 11 at 15:06:02 UTC; controlling SENT reply `1a12b8fa66d358d1`, 15:23:17 UTC. The original four messages were read directly. Correspondence stays with Bryce and its existing sender.

### MedStar / HealthLab: from study exports to an inspectable comparison

### The actual task and relationship

MedStar's [published Sovereign Execution project](https://healthit.gov/interoperability/investments/leap/2026-leap-in-health-it-projects) includes taxonomy-based shadow human-factors review against baseline workflows. In the actual October 12 reply, its investigator identified HealthLab as the technical partner and said she had shared the proposal. Bryce's approved follow-up asks to agree a defined implementation workshare with that technical lead.

The proposed unit remains **one installation, one study workflow, up to two agreed export families and one report/receiving format, for $12,000 in three $4,000 milestones over twenty business days after the agreed inputs and access are ready**. The current original conversation has no accepted scope, delivery dates, supplied study records, payment or Stellar-use agreement. The customer’s current manual effort and preferred replacement workflow have not been measured; the public project and our proposed integration are the sources of the workflow below.

The merged Study Operations Workspace and complete integration handover implement the adjoining task: import complete exports, select their interpretation, assign and adjudicate human review, compare the intended populations, and deliver the report with the state another operator needs to reopen it. The study owner defines the protocol and decisions; the technical partner defines the Bridge and export interfaces.

### What a complete study output means

|Stage|Study/operator decision|Original application object and receiving outcome|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|Original exports|Choose up to two complete agreed families, their exporter versions and actual relationship/time fields.|Original file plus source/extraction edition. FHIR resource IDs, Consent references, OTLP trace/span IDs and exact timestamps remain available.|
|Interpretation|Select the authoritative protocol, taxonomy and expected actions.|Frozen protocol and case versions. An imported row count does not stand in for the expected action population.|
|Review|Assign reviewers; save completion, routing, permission and transformation findings; adjudicate disagreements.|Attributed opinions and reasoned adjudication tied to the same case/action version. Later source or case changes leave prior opinions visible as prior evidence.|
|Comparison|Choose baseline and agent cases, comparable action keys/types and the actual study population.|Explicit one-to-one matches. Each dimension uses its jointly assessed population; missing, uncertain, disputed and stale findings remain visible.|
|Report|Select the protocol, cases, original evidence and intended recipient.|Frozen report JSON/CSV/HTML and complete report ZIP. Its original sources and decisions remain inspectable alongside the reported values.|
|Receiving|Open the delivered report, record the recipient's actual response and transfer the installation.|Original delivery/receipt plus complete private source/data backup and a restored editable workspace.|


This creates a precise acceptance walkthrough for the proposed workshare: the receiving operator follows one agreed source export through its mapping, reviews and adjudicates selected actions, reads the paired population, receives the frozen report and reopens the same work. A later export, reviewed protocol change or completed review period supplies a reason to produce a new report edition. Actual frequency, time saved and willingness to pay remain to be established with the client.

The software keeps different evidence in its own role. An original Task is a resource snapshot. A trace event is an observed event. A Consent object and a human authorization decision are separate. Native Solid access results describe the actual configured server permission observation; they do not supply a patient's authorization. The application records study operations and does not execute patient care.

### Proposed milestone delivery

|Original proposed milestone|Complete result under the existing offer|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|1 — $4,000|Installation, selected export mappings, protocol/taxonomy configuration and the agreed case/action population ready for the technical and study operators to inspect.|
|2 — $4,000|Reviewer assignment, independent findings, adjudication, authorization linkage and the selected baseline/agent comparison operated by the study reviewer.|
|3 — $4,000|Frozen report and receiving format, complete editable tables, source/data backup and the receiving operator's walkthrough.|


The original offer does not specify a delivery-hour estimate, so this contribution does not derive one from twenty business days or charge its $12,000 against the SCF packages.

The implemented application is pinned at `d0baf7f4f49bf34f890a7f6911942740c6c413fc`; its integration handover was merged by PR35396 at `5f6b4b58155234262a18aa562b3058848a2dafee`. The original publisher workflow retains 61 original files totaling 313,865 bytes with their source URLs, hashes and notices. The sole native programme remains `MEDSTAR-NATIVE-PUBLISHER-39DA-20261012`, owned by 39DA. The current read of its source/customer thread contains the existing receiving request and no complete native result. There is no study/report/backup ID in this contribution to substitute for that missing return. ### How this evidence improves the grant's delivery case

The two examples answer different questions. Veridex's human invitation identifies an external Stellar buyer integration and onboarding task. MedStar's referral identifies the real technical-partner relationship for a defined study/report workshare, while the implemented application demonstrates how its original data, decisions and receiving can stay together. The existing six packages provide the development allocation: customer source/runtime and receiving adaptations in T1; same-service testnet integration and deployed payment/delivery recovery in T2; production deployment, recurring mainnet use and independent maintenance in T3. The existing $38,000, 400 hours and 150-day plan remain unchanged. Any selected adaptation is assigned once to the grant or to the original commercial workshare. Already implemented general study software and uncommissioned sales work are not billed again as prospective Stellar engineering.

Useful measurement follows the actual customer operation. Retain the named operator and task, the selected input and complete output, active integration or review effort, actual corrections, receiving result and later source/request that creates a distinct new task. Keep purchased request counts beside completed parent tasks. A repeated file read, source move or resumed delivery continues its original result. The original SCF cohort model owns the independent operator, testnet/mainnet and repeat-purchase accounting.

## A2A analytical services: complete agent work, merchant delivery and customer receiving

An organisation commissioning an analytical service needs a useful operation that its staff and agent applications can repeat. A reporting team may select a new source edition, run an approved query over every observation, receive complete tables and reports, and hand the working analysis to another engineer. The merchant needs an exact result to publish, native payment terms and a recoverable release. The buyer needs the complete acquired output in its own application.

The installed A2A analytical product joins those tasks through one source selection. It contains the original Python Analysis Workspace, an analytical A2A service, a standard receiving client, the merchant Agent workspace, the original SF30 seller and SF82 release integration, and complete customer receiving commands. Its normal `a2a-analysis` product selection follows the maintained source builder and runtime installer. [Complete installed product](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/products/a2a-analysis/README.md)

### Accountable customer operation

A commissioned installation starts with the actual source and decision the customer needs. Its workorder names the commissioning payer, source owner, analytical service operator, merchant publishing the result, independent buyer and receiving engineer. One organisation may fill more than one role; the service's configuration and commercial agreement retain each authority.

The workorder defines the complete selected source edition, field and time meaning, authorised use and redistribution, saved query or report revision, permitted parameter inputs, full output formats, output limits, expected receiving application and acceptance owner. It identifies the priced unit: for example, one reviewed complete monthly report edition or a named result package. The later reporting period, changed source or distinct approved query supplies the reason for another purchase. Source licence, upstream service access and engineering fees remain recorded with that customer's agreement.

The analytical host captures selected saved queries and report definitions from its original workspace. A caller receives the procedures available to its configured principal. The captured selection retains the actual workspace and view identities, saved SQL or report revision and original parameter text. The customer application can therefore follow which source and procedure produced a delivered result. A deliberate source or procedure change receives a new reviewed selection while earlier task history remains available. [Analytical service and procedure authority](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/stellar-forge/a2a-analysis-agent/README.md)

### Source to complete result

The customer first registers the original acquisition, source document or received dataset in the Analysis Workspace, reviews its projection, imports the selected edition and saves the useful query or report. Its existing Python engine owns those source, SQL, report and export operations. The A2A service connects that application to the official A2A JavaScript SDK 1.3.0 and its original task persistence and event processing. The host selects stable principals, permitted procedures and environment-supplied credentials. [Installed operating flow](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/products/a2a-analysis/OPERATING.md) · [Pinned official SDK source](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-js/tree/29417a5bb4038f804f310ce4fffd267a9375aa90)

The merchant operator captures the real Agent Card, reviews its selected interface, saves the exact request and sends a catalogue or selected-procedure message. The task retains its original request, message, context and native job identities before effects. The operator can read or subscribe to the same task, reopen its saved state and continue an interrupted result. The browser retains pending request bytes and drafts; a delayed reply cannot silently substitute another project's selection. [Merchant Agent workspace](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/a2a/OPERATOR.md)

Query tasks return the selected complete CSV, JSONL and SQLite exports, the original manifest and an analytical record. Report tasks return the selected full JSON, HTML and CSV ZIP outputs with their original report and publication identities. Full-query completion is required; a preview row limit does not define the delivered population. Configured output limits produce an explicit failed task when the selected complete output cannot fit. When caller parameters are allowed, their original JSON text reaches Python unchanged, preserving integer values that a JavaScript number conversion could alter. [Complete native file contract](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/stellar-forge/a2a-analysis-agent/README.md#complete-customer-files)

Complete-result review binds every retained output to its original Task or Message part position and artifact identity. Inline text, data and raw files are checked against their original bytes. A configured URL output retains the selected URL and observed complete transfer. A receiver rejects missing, duplicated or extra outputs even if a packet claims to be complete. The reviewed result can then become a named immutable edition with its original filenames, media types, byte counts, hashes and task lineage. [Result receiving and exact output population](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/products/a2a-analysis/RECEIVING.md)

### Native payment and release authority

A2A supplies the upstream task and result interface. The merchant publishes the reviewed frozen result through the existing SF30 seller, which retains the network, asset, recipient, integer amount, challenge, verification and settlement records. The existing buyer controls approval, signing and aggregate spending. Its acquired file stays bound to that original paid publication.

The original SF82 release engine owns staging, activation, draining of accepted requests and rollback. An operator reads the current generation before applying the selected release change. An earlier acquired result and its terms remain inspectable after a later release. The Applications integration opens the same retained merchant workspace from its selected installed runtime and private connection configuration. [Merchant publication and release operation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/a2a/OPERATOR.md) · [Installed product commands](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/products/a2a-analysis/README.md#product-commands)

A settled purchase, a completed upstream task, a complete customer file and an accepted business handover have their own records. Funded receiving must join the approved paid request, native transfer, exact output and customer acceptance. The current A2A commissioning source includes an explicitly labelled `CHALLENGE_ONLY` publication exercise; its `verified: false` and `settled: false` values remain visible. That exercise adds no paid purchase to the existing register. [Original commissioning source](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/a2a/receiving/commission.mjs)

### Installation, recovery and independent handover

The receiving engineer builds one immutable source commit through the original distribution builder with `--selection a2a-analysis`. The original runtime installer receives the builder's actual archive and SHA-256, selects both `a2a` and `a2a-analysis` features, installs their shared SDK once and checks the actual SQLite binding. The installed source includes the analytical Python package, merchant browser, typed clients, CLI, systemd service and explicitly selected Nginx configuration. The receiving host supplies its own private data directories, credentials, HTTPS origin and service ownership. [Build and installation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/products/a2a-analysis/OPERATING.md#1-build-and-install-the-selected-source)

The unified `a2a-product` command forwards unchanged arguments to the original runtime, workspace, archive, agent, merchant and receiving modules. The Python workspace entry selects that installed source and Node executable and waits for the original Python owner to finish. A runtime upgrade retains its source and dependency comparison and uses the existing release and rollback controls. Both analytical and merchant components resolve the same selected runtime. [Unified source entry](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/products/a2a-analysis/cli.mjs) · [Python owner entry](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/products/a2a-analysis/python-command.mjs)

The customer receives the type of working material its agreement requires:

|Delivered work|Original receiving operation|What the customer retains|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|Analytical task and files|`a2a-product receive`|Agent Card, exact message, original task snapshots and every complete output file|
|Frozen purchased result|`a2a-product merchant inspect-result`|Reviewed edition, native task lineage and exact original output bytes|
|Editable merchant project|`a2a-product merchant receive`|Source review, project revisions, result editions, publications and named handoffs|
|Complete analytical workspace|`a2a-product archive receive`|Original database, retained sources, saved queries, reports and workspace identity|


Receiving the same packet reuses its saved result. A later compatible project carries its own history and earlier named handoffs; an older or divergent packet is identified against the current work. The receiving operator selects its own live host connection before making further upstream requests. Historical inspection and downloads remain bound to the selected revision. The analytical archive receiver checks the complete original members, resumes its own retained staging operation when necessary and publishes the restored workspace through the original engine. [Complete customer receiving guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/products/a2a-analysis/RECEIVING.md)

Recovery preserves the original operation. Losing a receiving stream leaves the service's background task persistence active. A service restart reopens the same task database, procedure selection and native job IDs. Repeated cancellation reconciles the saved native cancellation intent. The final handover retains actual failed, interrupted and unresolved outcomes alongside completed work, so a receiving engineer can finish the identified step. [Task, restart and cancellation contract](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4/stellar-forge/a2a-analysis-agent/README.md#resume-and-cancellation)

The selected complete product is commit `9106f038471ba9435f9600ccf5a090d97b6c84f4`. |T3 · Production recovery and handover|Restore the customer's retained analytical/merchant state and files on its receiving host, reconcile later operations and finish the independent maintainer's support case.|


The request remains **USD 38,000 / 400 hours / 150 days from award acceptance**, with the original tranche amounts, independent-use targets, cash assumptions and submission state. A customer agreement and actual commissioning acceptance are still required. A subsequent accepted source edition, report period or distinct query gives the funded buyer a useful reason to return.

### Customer commissioning calendar and complete useful jobs

The fourteen-day mainnet target needs an explicit customer calendar. On an ordinary Monday–Friday schedule without holidays, two buyers making one useful purchase each per business day produce twenty purchases in fourteen calendar days. The proposed commissioning calendar reaches thirty through fifteen independently useful jobs per buyer: ten complete source-period extracts and five separate reconciliation or reporting decisions. Both proposed merchant installations serve both buyers. The customer workorder must replace the relative dates, source periods and roles with actual customer selections before this plan can be used.

The [complete customer commissioning specification](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/33dfb64798f5316a586c165d4d7591de972ca4e2/stellar-forge/developer-site/A2A_CUSTOMER_COMMISSIONING.md) and [thirty-job register](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/33dfb64798f5316a586c165d4d7591de972ca4e2/stellar-forge/developer-site/a2a-customer-commissioning.json) name each job's purpose, period, complete output and receiving role. Buyer A's additional jobs cover new or missing observations, late corrections, asset coverage, metadata/status changes and a correction decision register. Buyer B's additional jobs deliver distinct two-period briefs, a source-quality publication, a complete first-workweek report, a selected-cohort report and a complete two-workweek publication. These are prospective customer adaptations to approved saved queries/reports; customer identities, procedure IDs, source licenses, prices, signers and receiving people remain unselected.

For each actual job, the receiving record joins the original customer approval, priced request, native settlement, A2A task, merchant request, full output byte identities and SF82 release/edition to the named receiver's decision. Useful customer jobs, priced requests, native settlements and complete received tasks are counted separately. Retries, reconnects, resumed work, several formats for one result and unnecessary repeat purchases do not create additional useful jobs. The existing development reference and team testnet baseline remain separately attributed.

The appendix preserves the existing $38,000-equivalent request, 400-hour allocation, 150-day programme and milestone definitions. Its remaining customer work fits once into the existing six funded packages, or into a separately commissioned workorder where applicable. Already completed reusable source is the selected starting component. The current manuscript and installation owners approve the actual calendar and accountabilities; this prospective plan records no executed customer outcome or payment.

## Municipal source operations, service reporting and reviewed GIS delivery

Municipal software teams need to carry a resident's original request through service triage, management reporting, GIS allocation, work-order review and a crew's return. [Connected Bits](https://connectedbits.com/) describes integration across municipal CRM, GIS, asset and work-order systems. Our six-application municipal suite provides a complete operating path for that implementation task and a concrete recurring-service candidate for the existing Stellar merchant architecture.

### Present operating product and source meaning

The merged [municipal installation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9802397ae6ed5653bbb6cbb972dcc0ef22f24317/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/open311/service-configuration/INSTALL.md) selects source operations, service performance, GIS handoff, request/work-order Follow-through, Field Desk and service configuration through `open311-service-configuration`. Each has an ordinary browser and installed CLI. Five desks expose typed merchant providers; reporting uses its browser, CLI and direct source SDK. Original source files and complete editable exports connect the separate saved workspaces; the receiving engineer can reopen their decisions and continue work.

The [complete suite operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9802397ae6ed5653bbb6cbb972dcc0ef22f24317/products/open311/OPERATING.md) takes the receiving engineer through the [selected six-application package](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9802397ae6ed5653bbb6cbb972dcc0ef22f24317/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/selections/open311-service-configuration.json), runtime preparation, runtime-workspace initialization and attachment, and each saved Applications entry. The [editable receiving guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9802397ae6ed5653bbb6cbb972dcc0ef22f24317/products/open311/RECEIVING.md) gives all six original workspace schemas, receiving commands and identity rules. The [workflow and source-format guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/9802397ae6ed5653bbb6cbb972dcc0ef22f24317/products/open311/WORKFLOWS.md) identifies the exact collection, report, analyst, dispatch, crew and configuration files used between desks. Export files are published completely to new destinations; an existing file is preserved. Reporting keeps its receiving workspace identity and records the original source workspace; the other five desks restore the original workspace identity. Each managed application binds the actual received directory and identity.

Source operations fix the provider query, creation or update interval and observation history. They retain every complete original page, capped parent, refined child and unresolved interval. Reporting uses those immutable collections with a named status/calendar/target profile and an explicit observation cutoff. Original expected dates remain distinct from the customer's target policy. GIS prepares GeoPackage, GeoJSON, CSV or editable JSON, receives an analyst's returned file and turns selected proposals into a reviewed destination package.

Follow-through adds the operational join between a request and a work order. It keeps their original identifiers, source editions, costs, geometry and date precision separate, exposes source changes and requires an explicit relationship decision. Reviewed assignments and returned proposals produce a complete approved dispatch. Field Desk receives that original dispatch, assigns crews and visits, issues a portable return package, retains attachments and exact resource quantities, and lets the supervisor resolve partial or overlapping returns before preparing an update package. Field activity remains separate from the source publisher's request status and the original approved action.

Service configuration supplies the agency implementation layer. It versions departments, named staff, role/group declarations, service categories and custom fields, exact source mappings, routing conditions, staff/resident messages and rollout phases. A whole-register preview binds one configuration version to the complete original request file. Conflicting or unresolved routes remain visible; reasoned record decisions retain their original source keys. Due dates use an explicitly selected agency time zone and local calendar. A declared deployed baseline supplies the migration comparison; a saved draft remains editable through a new version. The resulting implementation release carries the configuration, every routing row, rendered message previews, remaining decisions and application order.

These meanings address practical source differences. [Boston's provider](https://311.boston.gov/open311/docs) distinguishes created-date and changed-record feeds, native page limits and a ten-request-per-minute allowance. A closed source case retains its literal disposition note; a citation, referral or duplicate does not become an invented completed repair. Helsinki's processing statuses remain literal. Manatee's observed coordinate values and declared reference system remain in their source records. Omaha's generated object-ID changes remain distinct from business-field changes, and its date-only strings keep their actual precision.
