## Process, decision and adaptive-case commissioning with complete customer receiving

A merchant or implementation partner needs to deliver an operating workflow that another engineer can understand, run and continue. A process diagram alone does not carry the deployed definition, the business inputs, the decision outcome, the human work or the history needed to recover an interrupted operation. The maintained Flowable application brings that work together in one editable operating workspace.

An operator can deploy the original BPMN process, CMMN case and DMN decision resources; select their native editions; review a prepared request; perform the approved operation; inspect the engine's response and history; and deliver the complete workspace to an independent receiving installation. The industrial browser, installed command line, typed client, managed Applications and merchant agent connection operate the same saved records. The complete product exposes 45 workspace actions and 51 Flowable merchant tools.

The [process operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/cb95ff9198d4b1cdf554eb35eb16cbf3676a3857/products/flowable-merchant/OPERATING.md), [decision operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/cb95ff9198d4b1cdf554eb35eb16cbf3676a3857/products/flowable-merchant/DECISIONS.md) and [adaptive-case guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/cb95ff9198d4b1cdf554eb35eb16cbf3676a3857/products/flowable-merchant/CASES.md) describe the maintained implementation. The selected native contract is Flowable 8.0.0, source revision 0779d68e5a3385b74d8acb8bc37901ff54513249. Customer commissioning selects the actual engine service, authorized source resources, business identities and accountable operators.

### One customer operation from source to handover

Consider a proposed grant-review service whose buyer supplies an application and supporting records. A BPMN process can express the agreed sequence of intake, assessment and approval. A DMN decision table can evaluate the explicitly supplied criteria. A CMMN case can retain work that depends on missing documents, a specialist review or an exception in the evidence. Each native model keeps its own semantics and source edition. The installation records which process, decision or case the customer actually selected.

The authored source programme includes grant review, vendor review and onboarding examples with two source editions. Their purpose is to commission the implementation against explicit inputs and native outcomes. A customer's actual eligibility policy, approval authority, evidence and operating procedure are selected during the engagement. Human owners review policy and consequential decisions; the software retains the requests and results that those decisions produce.

The useful deliverable may be a completed reviewed case, an evaluation report, a versioned decision service, or the commissioned operating application and its customer handover. The workorder states what the buyer receives, the accepted input, the selected rules or process edition, the completion condition and the receiving owner. That selection is carried through source preparation, engine operation and the resulting files.

### Install and reopen the same application

The [selected installation guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/cb95ff9198d4b1cdf554eb35eb16cbf3676a3857/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/selections/FLOWABLE_MERCHANT.md) uses the existing distribution builder and runtime installer. Its flowable-merchant selection includes the original engine adapters, durable workspace, complete browser, typed client, CLI, merchant provider and customer receiving. Node 24 and Linux flock operate the workspace; the original native commissioning host uses Java 17 or later for Flowable.

The operator builds from a complete committed source revision, retains the selected archive and build result, installs that release, and initializes the private product directory. Existing native workspaces can be selected explicitly. Initial connection declarations name the actual process, case and decision REST services and the environment variables that supply their credentials. Saved connection revisions remain authoritative after initial setup.

Through Applications, the engineer selects the READY runtime, existing product directory and private environment file, then follows Review, Save, Start and Open. Startup checks the original product identity, actual listener, workspace UUID, connection record and browser source. Stop drains the same workspace before closing its writer. A later Start reopens the saved identity and current history. This supports an ordinary maintainable deployment in which the customer's working state survives application restarts and reviewed runtime upgrades.

### Release and operate a process edition

The process workspace captures the complete native portfolio, deployed source and active or historical work. The operator opens the original BPMN definition, prepares a release from its full resource or native deployment archive, and reviews the exact request and engine preimage before dispatch. A process start retains its business key, complete typed input and selected definition.

Human work uses the original task identity for claim, unclaim, delegation, resolution and completion. A migration retains Flowable's original migration document and native validation before dispatch, then reads the resulting definition, active work and history. The customer can compare the selected earlier and later editions without losing the original source or request.

An interrupted operation stays attached to its saved preparation, dispatch and native response. Reopening the application continues the original request. The operator reconciles an uncertain outcome through the retained record and engine readback. The source programme includes a deliberately interrupted accepted process-start response so the original receiving journey can demonstrate that the same business key retains one native process and one start dispatch.

### Evaluate decisions with their original typed input

The decision service has its own named native REST connection. The operator deploys a complete DMN resource, inspects the native definition and source, selects the required edition and prepares an evaluation with the original typed variables. The saved review retains the selected decision or decision service and exact request.

The application preserves original JSON numeric text, including long integer values that exceed JavaScript's exact numeric range. The readable interface accompanies the complete source bytes; it does not replace those values with a rounded reconstruction. Results and decision execution audits retain their native identity, response and input context. A second rule edition can be evaluated against the same authored business cases and compared as a separate selected source.

The customer receives the rules that were used and the resulting native history. Business-rule authors and accountable decision owners can therefore inspect an actual evaluation rather than relying on a summary detached from its definition or inputs.

### Continue adaptive cases and human work

The case workspace captures all eleven native collections: deployments, definitions, live cases, plan items, tasks, variables, historic cases, historic plan items, historic tasks, historic variables and milestones. Captures preserve complete pages, definition resources and available binary variable data. Saved portfolio revisions remain selectable after the application or engine restarts.

A CMMN release is prepared from the complete original resource. Starting by the actual caseDefinitionId selects a specific deployed version; starting by key uses the native matching definition retained in the preparation. The operator can update the case name or business key, ask the engine to evaluate criteria, or terminate selected live work while retaining its history.

Stages and plan items use their native start, trigger, enable and disable actions. The guide explicitly records that the pinned Flowable enable controller calls the native start operation. Human tasks use their actual case ownership and task IDs for claim, delegation, resolution and completion. Review displays original typed variables, the selected definition, related work and history.

The authored case programme includes grant diligence, vendor exceptions and onboarding investigations in two editable source editions. The installed continuation carries one original live case through SDK, CLI, merchant agent and browser operations, then completes and exports its history. Those surfaces share the original requests and records; they do not create separate copies of the customer's case.

### Commission an entire approved programme

The [Commissioning workspace](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/888cb09c514ac2f21f76b8b4eb5950eb50003a24/products/flowable-merchant/PROGRAMMES.md) turns an agreed sequence of native operations into a saved, source-complete programme within the existing application. An implementation partner can receive the customer's models and input edition, prepare the selected steps, inspect their native reviews, deliberately dispatch approved work and return the complete resulting history. The programme uses the same named connection, workspace lease, original operation records and customer receiving machinery as individual work.

The [original programme source contract](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/888cb09c514ac2f21f76b8b4eb5950eb50003a24/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/flowable/workspace/programme-core.mjs) carries every selected resource as complete bytes with its name, media type and content hash. It declares each native operation, its dependencies and the exact selection consumed by the existing process, decision or case planner. A programme selects one REST service family. A customer application that uses several services keeps separate saved programmes and their explicit connections.

The [saved programme operations](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/888cb09c514ac2f21f76b8b4eb5950eb50003a24/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/flowable/workspace/programmes.mjs) retain the full source edition and freeze each child preparation request, resolved input and binding evidence before invoking the original native model. Dependencies resolve only from confirmed earlier records. A binding selects an exact native string identifier from a retained response, preimage, readback or reconciliation record; an ambiguous row is rejected. Quoted identifier tokens can be replaced inside the original body text while every other byte remains unchanged. Exact long integer input therefore remains intact.

The [existing browser's programme controls](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/888cb09c514ac2f21f76b8b4eb5950eb50003a24/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/flowable/workspace/programme-browser.mjs) show the source members, ordered work, dependency readiness and actual native outcomes. The operator prepares a step and opens its existing native review and dispatch controls. After a lost preparation response, the saved child request resumes. Once a request was dispatched, an unknown outcome stays attached to that original record and is reconciled there. An undispatched stale or unsuccessful review may be deliberately renewed; preceding attempts remain in history.

Acceptance is a separate operator action. It requires every selected native step to be confirmed and binds the named reviewer, decision and note to the complete source and current record editions. If subsequent reconciliation creates another edition, the previous acceptance remains visible as an earlier review. It does not silently certify the changed result.

The [complete public reference programme](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/888cb09c514ac2f21f76b8b4eb5950eb50003a24/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/flowable/workspace/examples/case-commissioning.programme.json) includes ten original source members and 73 deliberate operations across grant diligence, vendor exceptions and onboarding investigation, with two model editions per family. It covers release, case start and criteria, manual review, claim and unclaim, delegation and resolution, source confirmation, an exception path and handover approval. The [maintained case compiler](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/888cb09c514ac2f21f76b8b4eb5950eb50003a24/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/flowable/workspace/case-programme.mjs) builds this format from complete selected cohort sources and accountable native user identities. These are editable commissioning examples; a customer approves its own policies, inputs, people and useful completion conditions.

The same four programme methods—save, read, prepare a step and record a review—are available in the typed client, ordinary CLI and merchant provider. Their declarations are in the [complete workspace action contract](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/888cb09c514ac2f21f76b8b4eb5950eb50003a24/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/flowable/workspace/actions.mjs) and [merchant catalogue](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/888cb09c514ac2f21f76b8b4eb5950eb50003a24/stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/catalog/flowable-workspace.mjs). The complete product has 45 workspace actions and 51 merchant tools. Those counts describe available interfaces, not completed customer operations or grant outcomes.

The [native programme receiving helper](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/888cb09c514ac2f21f76b8b4eb5950eb50003a24/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/flowable/workspace/native-programme-receiving.mjs) joins the already selected producer and independent receiving client. It retains the original request checkpoint, performs the selected native course through the existing controllers, stops on an unresolved outcome, then exports and downloads the whole workspace. The original receiver inspects and adopts that file and compares the received programme source and confirmed native outcome basis. The actual native owner retains the stopped receiver and cold-reopens that same workspace. This implementation is delivered source; the existing equipped-host operation must supply its real runtime and customer acceptance results.

### Receive the complete working history

The [customer receiving guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/cb95ff9198d4b1cdf554eb35eb16cbf3676a3857/products/flowable-merchant/RECEIVING.md) exports one frozen NDJSON workspace edition. It contains saved connection names, all record revisions, native sources, request and response bodies, original journals and receiving lineage, with complete member identities and a final digest. Saved connections carry credential-variable names; receiving hosts supply the corresponding secret values privately.

The installed client downloads the entire original file and checks its byte count and SHA-256. An interrupted download resumes against the same selected delivery identity and destination. The independent receiving application inspects the complete file, retains its manifest, adopts the exact reviewed history and cold reopens its own workspace UUID with the source provenance.

The receiving engineer can open the original definition, native operation review, case work, decision execution and full source resource. The same record and request histories remain available after reopening. Later approved work continues from that received state against the actual selected engine. A complete application transfer therefore includes both the editable product/source edition and the customer's full operating history.

### Native commissioning and source authority

The [original native receiving programme](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/cb95ff9198d4b1cdf554eb35eb16cbf3676a3857/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/flowable/NATIVE_RECEIVING.md) combines the complete process, decision and case journeys with installed browser, SDK, CLI, Applications and MCP operation. The [installed receiving implementation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/888cb09c514ac2f21f76b8b4eb5950eb50003a24/products/flowable-merchant/native-installed-journey.mjs) retains original inputs and outputs throughout that course. The [complete typed client contract](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/888cb09c514ac2f21f76b8b4eb5950eb50003a24/products/flowable-merchant/client.d.mts) exposes the same selected operation and receiving identities to an integration engineer.

The current full source programme contains 628 original files at installed source revision 24272d9d3ac3a19586769518fb25437cc28568e6. Its complete source, original Git tree and selected module closure have been received. The process, decision and adaptive-case implementation is merged in the maintained public and installed repositories. The existing native operation is continuing the complete engine and customer receiving course on equipped compute; that operation's actual returned results will supply the completed runtime edition.

The subsequent complete operator-programme capability is merged in public PR3323 and installed PR1257. Its public source edition is 888cb09c514ac2f21f76b8b4eb5950eb50003a24; the complete guides, programme, native receiving helper and client editions cited here were read back in full. The 73-step reference is an authored operating programme, and no completed engine run or customer acceptance is inferred from its source. This gives the reviewer concrete implementation and an executable operating path while the existing native commissioning continues. Future result updates belong to the same programme and customer workspace.

### Work within the six funded packages

The Flowable application is an existing implementation resource for a selected Stellar service installation. The grant's six packages continue to total USD 38,000, 400 prospective hours and 150 days from actual award acceptance. A selected workorder allocates the remaining installation work once within those packages.

| Existing package | Customer work performed for a selected workflow service | Acceptance material |
| --- | --- | --- |
| T1 resource integration, 80 hours | Select the useful buyer task, original process/case/rule source, permitted inputs, resulting artifact and merchant service interface. | Reviewed workorder, source edition, request/result contract and working merchant-resource integration. |
| T1 authority and handover, 40 hours | Establish customer policy and operating responsibility, select actual engine/task identities and transfer the complete application to the second operator. | Named owners, retained configuration, editable source and second-operator receiving. |
| T2 provider and ledger deployment, 70 hours | Join the chosen service to its original payment, provider and ledger deployment and handle actual buyer requests and delivered results. | Useful buyer purchases with original service requests, results and payment/ledger records. |
| T2 deployed threat response, 50 hours | Operate the installation's agreed response cases and recover an interrupted service or engine request through its original identity. | Actual response and reconciliation records from the selected installed service. |
| T3 mainnet merchant rollout, 90 hours | Put the agreed useful service into mainnet merchant operation and support repeat customer use. | Original merchant, buyer, purchase and returned-use records. |
| T3 production recovery and handover, 70 hours | Restore and reconcile the deployed service, reopen complete customer history and hand it to the receiving engineer. | Full application/source/workspace delivery and the receiving engineer's actual continuation. |

The overall targets remain two independent merchants and second-operator handover by day 30; two independent buyers and at least ten useful testnet purchases across seven consecutive calendar days by day 90, alongside the existing facilitator and response targets; and two mainnet merchants with at least thirty useful purchases across fourteen consecutive days by day 150, with both buyers returning on another day and an engineer restoring and reconciling the deployment.

Counting follows the buyer's useful purchased task. Model editions, internal engine calls, human task transitions, 51 available agent tools and repeated recovery observations are implementation activity. They do not multiply the original purchase. A workflow service selected for this programme retains the existing buyer/payment/result linkage so grant reporting can trace useful delivered work and repeat use.

### Delivery ownership and commercial continuation

The product supports an implementation partner that needs configurable workflow software, original source and a receiving engineer who can continue the deployment. A scoped engagement names its actual models, environment, decision owners, integrations, training and acceptance outputs. Separately priced partner engagements retain their own commercial plans and delivery hours.

The grant's remaining work is the selected Stellar installation and its observed customer adoption, deployment and recovery. The product chapter, original source declaration and customer operating guide enter the same maintained application, reviewer companion and source index. The existing submission workspace then carries them through its saved draft, review, Page and Site editions.

## Research quotations, paid delivery and complete customer programmes

A research agency needs a repeatable way to quote an evidence service, perform the work, deliver a useful result and continue with the customer's corrections. The implemented Research product keeps that complete operation in one customer programme. Its [quotation workspace](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4cd7288a061bb8943619804f8211916f881e7c28/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli/research-dossiers/customer-quotes/OPERATING.md) joins the original commercial case to observed supplier costs and pricing, a reviewed Research brief, source-linked customer work, a frozen delivery and the realized delivery report. The analyst and customer continue the same case and dossier histories as the service changes.

### Commission and price the actual service

The [Applications commissioning workflow](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4cd7288a061bb8943619804f8211916f881e7c28/products/research/COMMISSIONING.md) selects the real case store, Research workspace, pricing observations, delivery host and existing source connections. Preparation retains those complete selections for review; saving produces the original launch and Applications settings. The managed application can start, stop and reopen that same workspace. A selected source or configuration change returns to the maintained review path.

Within the customer case, the operator prepares the research brief from the agreed quote and chooses the actual dossier, project and source revision. The customer-response stage records the requested continuation against those originals. Quotation and pricing remain editable native commercial work; the programme records each complete request and displayed review before applying the selected action. This connects the agreed scope and price to the work that is actually delivered.

### Publish the selected result and receive the whole customer work

The [paid publication and Buyer workflow](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4cd7288a061bb8943619804f8211916f881e7c28/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli/research-dossiers/customer-commerce/OPERATING.md) freezes the selected Research delivery before registering it with the existing merchant. It retains the exact original publication, customer handoff and archive. The Buyer uses its configured account, approval and execution flow to retrieve that selected delivery, then receives the original dossier through the maintained Research receiver. Cancellation and lost-response recovery stay attached to that same original purchase and receiving operation.

The [complete programme and receiving workflow](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4cd7288a061bb8943619804f8211916f881e7c28/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli/research-dossiers/customer-quotes/PROGRAMME.md) carries every selected quotation operation, original phase input, native pricing and supplier-cost file, complete commercial case, source-bearing dossier, work snapshot and all four report formats. A completed paid publication contributes its exact published files and archive to that handover. The receiver reviews the original case transfer against the selected destination revision and retains the complete source package before applying it. The customer's received case and dossier are editable, with the commercial, service and Research histories needed for subsequent work.

The original request identities and review decisions remain useful after interruption or later peer edits. Completed requests reopen their saved result; continued work uses the received destination identities. The full file roster and original semantic receivers validate the selected package, including large native case records.

### Operate the same programme across the customer's tools

The browser, [installed Python interface and receiving example](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4cd7288a061bb8943619804f8211916f881e7c28/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli/python/RESEARCH-QUOTE-PROGRAMMES.md), [Merchant operations](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4cd7288a061bb8943619804f8211916f881e7c28/stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/RESEARCH_PROGRAMMES.md) and [installed remote terminal](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4cd7288a061bb8943619804f8211916f881e7c28/stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/RESEARCH_PROGRAMME_TERMINAL.md) use these same native engines. An analyst can work in the browser, another operator can continue a reviewed step from Python or the terminal, and an agent can operate the retained programme through the Merchant interface.

The remote terminal selects the original source and customer connections, retains complete input files, submits or resumes the existing jobs, exports every selected handover file and transfers the archive in exact resumable chunks. The receiving operator imports that whole archive, reviews the destination selection, receives the original case and dossier, and reopens them for the next service edition. Accepted cross-workspace work drains during Stop; interrupted file and upload operations continue from their original retained selections.

### Commissioning within the existing funded plan

A specific installation identifies the recurring research question, allowed source connections, named reviewer, customer case, pricing basis, report cadence and receiving organization. The useful customer outcome is an evidence service whose scope and quote lead to a delivered, editable programme that another operator can continue. Commissioning validates that selected customer's source and account configuration, approval path, full delivery and independent receiving.

This implemented workflow supplies a concrete T1 merchant-resource integration and authority/handover candidate within the existing six funded packages. T2 and T3 retain their existing independent receiving, repeat-purchase and production-handover outcomes. The canonical USD 38,000, 400-hour and 150-day proposal remains the controlling future delivery plan.

The merged browser, Python, native programme, Merchant and terminal source is available in the linked complete operating guides. The original selected-NCT installed receiving remains with its existing equipped operation and saved workspaces; its actual returned result supplies the deployment evidence for that specific customer journey.

## Grant reporting from original cases to received procedures

Grant Reporting turns an existing managed Grant Operations case and its complete Source Tables project into a reusable reporting procedure. The operator keeps the case's real work, invoices, cash, awards, deployments, purchases and outcomes, selects the reporting period, and prepares the original tools needed to inspect, report, export and hand over that work. A second operator can receive the complete procedure and its source material through the existing Grant case workflow. This gives a customer a repeatable reporting process whose source selections and later revisions remain inspectable.

The [complete creator and capture guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/b2b6efba94ffb5876a5f207b1f84e6ebf8c2117a/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/discovery/GRANT_REPORTING.md) documents the available implementation. The native capture source was merged in [Merchant PR1035](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/1035). The implementation is available; the selected native capture and two-operator receiving remain pending with their original operators. Completion will be recorded from their actual case, saved results and receiving records. Reporting instructions, authored status, customer acceptance and observed financial transfers retain their separate meanings.

### Prepare one real reporting period

In the existing Command finder, the customer opens **Operating plans → Create Grant reporting plan**. They select the complete original Grant case JSON or native show response, the complete Source Tables project, and the installed toolkit's complete catalog. They enter the title, customer, period, owner and receiving notes, the reporting end date, and an optional start date. Omitting the start date retains cumulative reporting. The workspace, source-project, report-output and receiving-workspace paths refer to the actual operating host; choosing a file in a browser does not establish its native path. The Command finder address remains the selected loopback HTTP address with an explicit port.

The [original-input validator](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/b2b6efba94ffb5876a5f207b1f84e6ebf8c2117a/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/discovery/grant-reporting-input.mjs) retains the case ID, version, mode, plan ID, selected plan revision and full planning snapshot. The Source Tables project must belong to that plan. Its selected table editions, mappings, reviews, workbook selections and baseline remain present. A baseline that is older than the case's selected plan stays visible as an explicit difference; preparation does not silently rebase it. Catalog registration must include the existing Grant workspace, Source Tables and discovery commands. Changing to the current installed catalog is a deliberate selection, including removal of stale source-checkout context when appropriate.

Preview creates the [canonical Operating Plan](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/b2b6efba94ffb5876a5f207b1f84e6ebf8c2117a/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/discovery/grant-reporting-core.mjs). The plan contains the original case and source-review steps together with the existing reporting procedure. Its steps start planned and its recorded results start empty, ready for the operator to record actual work. The customer downloads the complete preparation JSON to retain entered values, full original files, catalog and preview together. Reopening that preparation keeps its plan identity and UTC creation time; copying it for a new period creates a separate preparation. JSON, HTML and Markdown handovers describe the same canonical plan.

### Capture and reopen the selected managed case

The [installed reporting command](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/b2b6efba94ffb5876a5f207b1f84e6ebf8c2117a/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/discovery/grant-reporting-plan-cli.mjs) supports a native capture from the original managed Grant workspace. The operator selects the actual case ID and, when required, its expected version; supplies the complete Source Tables JSON, report fields and catalog or selected source checkout; and chooses a new output directory. An optional procedure selection names the original actor, note, selected revision, preceding source and explicit source, table, edition and step links.

Use the existing private client binding and the selected case's actual ID and reviewed version for these commands. Replace the example absolute paths with the original input and destination paths. The complete report-fields JSON requires `id`, `title`, `asOfDate`, `receivingWorkspace` and `commandFinderUrl`; use the actual reporting date and current loopback listener. Optional `savedAt` retains a chosen UTC plan creation time, and `startDate` sets the beginning of the reporting period. The catalog argument selects the complete installed catalog JSON.

```sh
starforge grant-reporting-plan capture \
  --binding /absolute/private/original-client.json \
  --case "$GRANT_CASE_ID" \
  --expected-version "$GRANT_CASE_VERSION" \
  --source-project /absolute/inputs/planning-source-project.json \
  --input /absolute/inputs/report-fields.json \
  --catalog /absolute/inputs/selected-toolkit-catalog.json \
  --out /absolute/reports/period-01

starforge grant-reporting-plan capture-show \
  --directory /absolute/reports/period-01
```

Choose an existing parent directory and a new capture destination. For a toolkit loaded from its selected checkout, replace `--catalog` with `--source-root /absolute/checkout --selection PRODUCT`, using that installation's actual product selection. To prepare the subsequent case attachment during capture, add `--procedure-selection /absolute/inputs/procedure-selection.json` with the original reviewed procedure choices.

The [native capture implementation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/b2b6efba94ffb5876a5f207b1f84e6ebf8c2117a/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/discovery/grant-reporting-native.mjs) reads the full selected case through the original client and binds the parsed case to its retained native bytes. It validates the same source project and catalog used by the creator, then rebuilds the canonical plan from those complete inputs. It reads the case again and checks the selected source files before completing the capture. A changed case, changed selected source or mismatched expected version requires reconciliation of that actual selection. Capture preserves the original case while producing a separate complete preparation for the subsequent save and receiving workflow.

A completed capture directory contains `reporting-preparation.json`, `grant-reporting-plan.json`, `grant-reporting-plan.html`, `grant-reporting-plan.md` and `capture.json`; an explicitly requested original procedure preparation adds `grant-procedure.json`. The capture manifest is written after the other outputs and binds their exact bytes. The client closes the connection or the service it owns before publishing completion, preserving any closure failure. An existing destination is not overwritten.

The customer can use `capture-show` to reopen the frozen capture without contacting the live case. It verifies the complete selected files and their hashes, reconstructs the plan from the retained preparation, and checks the case, source, plan and optional procedure bindings. Moving the directory does not rewrite the operating paths recorded inside it. An intended path or reporting-period change belongs in a new preparation. An interrupted directory remains available for diagnosis; the presence of some output files is insufficient to call its capture complete.

### Save, export, receive and return the procedure

The [original Grant procedure workflow](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/b2b6efba94ffb5876a5f207b1f84e6ebf8c2117a/stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace/GRANT_PROCEDURES.md) saves an Operating Plan in the existing case as an immutable source edition. The operator supplies the real actor and current case version. The selected request identity and complete prepared input are retained before dispatch. After an uncertain response, the operator resumes that same request and checks its original result. The retained request ID, prepared file and operation directory keep that recovery tied to the original save.

Procedure links distinguish the selected case plan, case source, local original file and preceding procedure. Source Tables and native Installation or Customer Task Outcome selections retain their actual IDs and revisions, complete selected responses and explicit step relationships. A step marked complete by an author remains distinguishable from a native execution result. Opening an unchanged procedure retains its original plan; an actual edit creates a later revision while keeping earlier sources and history.

The [complete receiving workflow](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/b2b6efba94ffb5876a5f207b1f84e6ebf8c2117a/stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace/GRANT_PROCEDURES_RECEIVING.md) exports the original case, Operating Plan, procedure, native plan, selected tables and editions, readable HTML/Markdown, source links and manifests. Export checks the selected case version around its work and publishes only a complete verified selection. The independent receiver uses the existing Grant importer and retains its actual destination case and plan mappings. Returned changes create a later procedure edition with an explicit predecessor. Reopening the first edition and the returned edition must preserve their respective source selections and histories. Missing predecessors or conflicting chains remain unresolved until the original records are reconciled.

Customer acceptance therefore follows an observable journey: select a real case and report period; reopen the complete preparation; capture and verify the original selection; save the original procedure; export and independently receive it; make an attributed change; receive the returned edition; and reopen both histories. The original operation records establish which steps actually occurred. The receiving operator records the actual destination, changed edition, reopened history and customer acceptance in that original operation.

## Mobility and education managed workbenches

Two original staff products now use the same maintained source, Workshare, Installation, Applications and Merchant foundation. The mobility product carries complete monthly publications into comparisons and source-backed findings. The education product carries exact course, pathway and framework editions into reviews and corrective actions. Each retains its own original workspace identity, source records and business history.

### Mobility source review

### Customer work and useful result

A mobility team needs to understand a complete published operating period before it can use the data in a service review or implementation decision. The useful unit of work is a reviewed source edition and its resulting analysis: the complete monthly publication, explicit field interpretation, retained quality findings, a comparable-period analysis, station flows, working review notes and the editable delivered workspace.

The implemented mobility workbench carries those pieces in one source-based staff application. It preserves the original published bytes alongside the selected import interpretation and records. Operators can reopen the precise edition that produced a finding, compare selected imports, inspect station flow and maintain review notes with complete record history. Markdown and CSV reports are accompanied by the complete runnable workspace archive.

The Installation profile is `mobility-source-review`; the managed Applications entry is `partner-mobility`. Their maintained source is [the full mobility workorder profile](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/ae97decd04f04b2ffc1989498140c9cbefec502e/stellar/scf_2026/sf49_data_commissioning/installation-workorders/mobility-source-review.json). The profile describes the original customer course, source population, useful output, receiving procedure, maintenance ownership and repeat trigger. The commissioned scope is supplied by the selected original Workshare.

### Original source and period interpretation

The original source product retains full monthly mobility publications and their source metadata. Import interpretation belongs to the original product; the managed integration receives its complete application and archived state. The source URL, file identity, selected field mapping, calendar period, import identity and original record history remain available together.

A comparison selects between two and twelve actual retained imports. The analysis uses the original product's calendar-day method and station-flow calculation. The comparison output keeps its selected import IDs so an operator can distinguish a source revision, another city or another month from a change in the analytical result. Review notes retain the supporting source and revision that the operator actually selected.

The original source/browser programme selects complete Oslo and Bergen September 2026 monthly publications. It receives them into the original product before any installation handover. That defined receiving programme is the source of its future measured row totals, source response identities and native outcomes; those counts are not inferred from the installed adapter.

|Working item|Retained meaning|Operator use|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|Monthly source edition|Complete original file, source metadata and selected interpretation|Reopen and inspect the publication used by the analysis|
|Import|Original import identity, mapped fields, valid and invalid rows and period|Review the complete intake and quality findings|
|Comparison|Explicit selected import IDs and original calculation|Compare actual periods and inspect the difference|
|Station analysis|Original source-backed station flows|Examine the selected import without mixing a later edition|
|Review note|Original source linkage, record ID and complete revision history|Record and revise findings with their supporting context|
|Delivery|Original report, CSV and full runnable workspace/application|Hand useful work to an independent operator|


### Commercial work becomes an original Installation

The generic profile receives the actual Workshare, phases, funding choices, acceptance checks and source-use decisions from the existing case. A commission is prepared through [the maintained partner commissioner](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/ae97decd04f04b2ffc1989498140c9cbefec502e/products/partner-workspace/commission.mjs), which reads the original Installation seed, original bindings and exact source selection.

The commissioner checks that the selected case and Workshare case match the original seed, that the source attachment is present in the same original bindings, and that the full source manifest belongs to the mobility product. It calls the existing profile loader and Installation preparation function. The prepared workorder, Workshare and checks are compared with the original seed before the complete output is published.

The output includes the unchanged original seed, bindings and source selection, the prepared Installation document and preview, the whole workorder, and the exact native preparation request. The original operator uses the maintained preview/save flow. Private company fees, contacts and original commercial dates remain in that selected case; the reusable profile supplies the product and receiving procedure.

A source fee, merchant purchase or Stellar-funded activity remains part of the original selected commercial work. The actual authorization, payer, price, source output and receiving check must be present in that case when used. The mobility adapter itself operates the retained application and source records; a file count or retry is not a new commercial unit.

### A complete mobility course

1. Select the original Workshare and Installation case, its source bindings and the complete original runtime manifest. Select the saved original workspace archive when continuing an existing case.
2. Prepare the immutable source edition and original workspace with one retained request ID. Inspect the product, source identity and workspace UUID.
3. Save and review the Mobility source review entry in Applications, start the original server and open its actual local URL.
4. Inspect original publications, their field interpretation and source quality. Select the actual comparable imports; inspect calendar-day comparison and station flows.
5. Create or revise the original source-backed finding in the staff editor, inspect its complete history, and retain the useful original report and CSV.
6. Stop and reopen the same managed entry, confirming that the selected original workspace and records persist.
7. Stop the application for a complete original workspace export and installation snapshot. Retain the exact original request IDs and output identities.
8. Independently receive the complete installation, open the mobility application under its new installation identity and original workspace UUID, inspect the retained records and continue ordinary work.
9. Export onward from that received installation, keeping the original source, edited state and prior installation lineage.

This course follows the original product's APIs. The integration adds no parallel source store, note database or business queue.

### Education quality review

### Customer work and useful result

An education team needs a review that can be reopened against the exact course, pathway, framework and evidence it assessed. The useful result includes the original publication facts, the selected edition of every pathway member, criterion decisions and reasoning, source-linked corrective actions, complete history and a runnable editable handover.

The implemented education workbench carries course and pathway records, framework criteria, reviews and corrective actions in one staff application. Reviews retain their exact parent course and framework revisions. Pathway reviews additionally retain the full selected child-course revision map and complete child snapshots. A later change can therefore be shown as a change in the reviewed context instead of silently altering what an earlier review meant.

The Installation profile is `education-quality-review`; the managed Applications entry is `partner-education`. Their maintained source is [the full education workorder profile](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/ae97decd04f04b2ffc1989498140c9cbefec502e/stellar/scf_2026/sf49_data_commissioning/installation-workorders/education-quality-review.json). The original customer Workshare supplies the actual scope, source rights, commercial assignments and acceptance decisions.

### Original publications and exact review context

Course records preserve original availability and complete publication facts. A listing, removed course, revised publication and an operator's review decision have different meanings. The editor retains the saved availability value rather than upgrading a published listing when unrelated fields change.

The original education source programme includes nine course slots and two pathways from the selected publications. It preserves the explicitly removed Digital Twin course and original differences between provider and Campus descriptions, durations and certificate conditions. Those source facts are retained separately from review conclusions. Provider certificate conditions remain publication facts; learner issuance and programme eligibility require their actual responsible process.

A review selects the actual course/pathway edition and framework edition. For a pathway it also selects every current child course revision. The application keeps the exact map and full child snapshots with the saved review. Its current-context display shows when a parent, framework or child edition has changed. Starting a current-edition review is an explicit operator action; the older review and its original evidence remain intact.

Corrective actions bind to an exact review ID and revision. The staff interface displays that linkage and offers an explicit current-review selection when an action needs to move to a later review. Existing actions retain their original linkage until the operator changes it. A concurrent edit cannot silently rebind a saved action to a different review.

|Course publication|Complete original facts, availability, evidence and record revision|Compare a current publication with the originally reviewed edition|
|Pathway|Original membership and selected member revisions|Review the complete course group and identify changed or removed members|
|Framework|Exact criteria and saved framework revision|Explain the requirements actually used in a review|
|Review|Parent/framework revisions, child snapshots, criterion decisions and evidence|Reopen the same assessment and explicitly begin its successor|
|Corrective action|Exact review revision, owner, date, status and note history|Continue follow-up without changing the original assessment context|
|Delivery|Whole review report, CSV and complete original runnable workspace|Transfer the editable reviewed work and its supporting source|


### Staff editor and interrupted work

The complete staff editor preserves working drafts and their source contexts while a user moves between records. A review draft's context includes the complete child revision map. Returning to another edition restores that draft's actual inputs; selecting the current context is explicit.

Saved revisions and action updates use the original expected revision. When a response is interrupted, the client inspects the actual saved history and compares the complete intended body before receiving that result. Concurrent changes remain available for review against the original base. History, source evidence and complete archive downloads use the original application APIs.

The receiving procedure exercises both the initial review and a current-edition successor, then the original action and an independent restored edit. Its receiver checks both complete preserved history and every original current record head. A received record cannot disappear or rewind to an older saved revision merely because that earlier revision remains in history.

The implementation is part of the maintained merchant workspace at [the complete operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/ae97decd04f04b2ffc1989498140c9cbefec502e/products/partner-workspace/SCF.md). The application is prepared from a complete original runtime manifest, including its license and relative dependencies. Every member has its original byte count and SHA-256. The preparation copies those exact files into an immutable edition and restores a selected original whole-workspace archive, or intentionally creates the original empty workspace.
