A stopped application can adopt a complete runtime successor against the same saved workspace. Earlier source editions and the exact original named operation remain available. Whole workspace export carries runnable application source, the database snapshot and selected original objects. The additional installation ZIP carries all source editions and lifecycle lineage. Independent receiving assigns a new installation UUID, preserves the original workspace UUID and reopens the actual application. A further export and receiving step carries that history onward.

The current source includes the complete original-to-installed receiving programme. It selects the existing source programme's final independently edited archive by default, validates every source and archive member, prepares the managed application, exercises its actual interface, exports useful original outputs, independently receives the installation and reopens it, and performs onward export. The same-case receiver retains its original operation, inputs, request IDs and current attempt result across interruption. Its source is published; the original source/browser programme and this installed continuation await their equipped host's actual execution. The grant's operating evidence should advance from that original result when returned.

## OAuth resource operations and complete customer support

### Customer purpose and delivery

An API operator needs to distinguish an unavailable authorization dependency from an access decision that correctly refused a caller. The OAuth Support contribution connects that operational question to the existing customer case: inspect the original protected resource, retain its source observations, review the original incident, assign a repair to its owner, compare a later source, and hand the complete case to another operator.

The customer uses the existing Merchant Support application and original SF93 incident service. This contribution adds OAuth observations to those tools; it does not introduce another identity provider, verifier, incident controller, customer case store or billing system. The customer receives the original source files, case notes, before/after evidence, readable report and portable handoff. The implementation belongs within the application's existing technical implementation, service and customer receiving work.

The complete feature is merged in [PR893](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/893) at `39d1b70146e92a779dc024842a075f951b4e5943`; the installed operator and types are merged in [PR1022](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/1022) at `d49f7be36d3cf06ccb85e0eb6d6fcb410a46e02d`. Full native acceptance continues through the original programme and its returned customer-receiving artifacts.

### Select the existing authority

The operator opens **Applications → Merchant support → Incidents** and selects a named OAuth source from the customer's private incident-source profile. The original protected observation endpoint uses the resource's existing JWT authentication and tool authorization, including its host-authority callback. The original operator credential is supplied through a private environment reference; its value is not entered into this browser form or included in the handoff.

The operator selects the existing watcher revision, inspects the named resource, and reviews its resource identity, configuration digest, session, authority and observer state. Only that reviewed response can be adopted into the original configuration draft. Editing the selection or receiving a response for an older revision invalidates adoption. Applying the draft and starting or stopping observation continue through the original incident manager.

The [complete console guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/d49f7be36d3cf06ccb85e0eb6d6fcb410a46e02d/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/OAUTH_SUPPORT.md) explains the actual alias, revision and source lifecycle. The [original MCP operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/d49f7be36d3cf06ccb85e0eb6d6fcb410a46e02d/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/OAUTH_MCP.md) exposes the same flow to a tool-using operator: discover the existing Support inventory, read the current incident profile, then call `merchant_support_oauth_inspect` with a registered source ID and expected configuration revision. The browser and MCP tool cannot choose an arbitrary observation endpoint or substitute a credential reference.

### Keep the observed decision units

The original observation has separate authentication, tool-authorization, host-authority and issuer-key stages. Each records starts, completions, allowed, denied, unavailable and failed checks together with exact outcome codes. These are checks, not distinct HTTP requests, API transactions or sales. One resource request can invoke more than one stage. The monitoring call and its own key and host-authority checks are excluded from operational counters by the original host's observation context.

Normal `INVALID_TOKEN`, `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` and `ACCESS_DENIED` outcomes remain visible enforcement. They do not become an outage or a request to relax the original authority. An actual `HOST_ERROR` records an exception from the original callback. Key-fetch availability is recorded separately from the verifier's decision to accept a key or token.

The [original observation contract](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/d49f7be36d3cf06ccb85e0eb6d6fcb410a46e02d/stellar-forge/mcp-paid-agent/oauth-observation-contract.mjs) retains the session, capture time, sequence, resource/configuration binding, configured issuer metadata, key-cache state, stage counters, minute rows and exact outcomes. It excludes bearer tokens, subject values and tool arguments. Configured issuer addresses, permitted scope metadata, tool names and allowlist counts may still be operationally sensitive; the operator reviews the case's intended recipient.

Missing observations remain missing. A failed source read carries its original error and a null source, rather than invented zero activity. The [original codec and condition classifier](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/d49f7be36d3cf06ccb85e0eb6d6fcb410a46e02d/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf93-seller-support-bundle/oauth-observation.mjs) validates the complete file pair and recomputes its summary. The source pair is `oauth-observation.json` plus `oauth-source.json`; the latter retains the original observation bytes or the original failed-read null value.

### Turn a real incident into useful customer work

The existing watcher evaluates actual source failures, changed configuration, inconsistent evidence, incomplete observer state, unavailable verification, host-authority errors and issuer-key availability or rate limiting. The customer queue uses that same classifier. A quiet key cache or unknown condition does not create an extra repair job.

The case identifies the relevant owner and evidence before a repair is undertaken:

|Observed condition|Useful customer action|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|The selected source cannot be read|Reconcile the original endpoint, observation permission, credential reference and read deadline with its operator.|
|Resource or authority configuration changed|Review the changed identity before updating its saved registration.|
|Source continuity or observer coverage is incomplete|Retain the limitation and resolve the original lifecycle or source mismatch before using a comparison.|
|The original verifier or host callback is unavailable or throws|Work with its existing owner and retained diagnostics; keep the original authority requirements.|
|The configured issuer-key service is unavailable or rate-limited|Restore its original dependency or respect the original cooldown; retain the actual key-fetch response category.|


The workflow does not prove that a proposed repair caused a later change. It preserves the action and later observation so a human can assess them. Recovery requires the original classifier's fresh complete window and successful checks; a restart, empty window or absence of new failures does not establish recovery.

An operator opens the original incident as a customer case, retains its before/after captures and metadata, records the owner and next action, and saves the case using the existing CaseStore revision rules. The [complete customer receiver](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/d49f7be36d3cf06ccb85e0eb6d6fcb410a46e02d/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/oauth-receiving.mjs) operates these same incident-to-case, runtime inspection, export and import APIs. It does not manufacture an incident or acknowledge one again during receiving.

### Compare only compatible observations

The Support report shows both original observations and their exact files. A cumulative check interval requires the same reviewed selection, resource, configuration, session and session start, increasing snapshot sequence, nondecreasing capture time and cumulative counters, and retention of earlier issuer buckets. Separate sessions or mismatched identities remain separate evidence.

A compatible comparison reports per-stage cumulative differences and outstanding checks at both ends. A newly observed issuer has no observed earlier bucket, so its interval is left unobserved. The generic HTTP request interval remains empty for this source type. The before and after minute windows can overlap and are never added together to manufacture incremental activity.

The before-source repair queue remains a historical source-bound view even when the later source recovers. The report labels which source produced each observation and action. This lets a receiving operator see the original problem, the recorded intervention and the later evidence without rewriting history.

### Deliver and reopen the complete case

The original portable handoff retains the complete workspace text, runtime text, source bytes, selected mapping and human case metadata. Its read-only HTML report includes authority, check counts, exact outcomes, file identities, comparison and actionable queue. Opening that report does not fetch the observation endpoint or send credentials.

The receiving operator imports the exact selected handoff and saves it under the same stable case ID in the existing CaseStore. Source and received stores retain their own actual revisions; fresh import is not represented as a copy of all source-store timestamps or history. A lost save acknowledgment is reconciled by reading the original case and retained versions. If a later case head exists, the receiver retains that head and locates the original selected version rather than overwriting newer work.

The original [receiving guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/d49f7be36d3cf06ccb85e0eb6d6fcb410a46e02d/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/OAUTH_RECEIVING.md) defines the complete source selection, artifacts, listener ownership and actual completion receipts. Its independent reopening compares the received case, reproduced handoff and readable report with the frozen originals. Browser screenshots and viewport measurements are separate optional observations, not an accessibility certification.

### Carry the case into the customer's operating plan

The same customer case can now become a practical procedure for the next operator. The complete Support Operating Plans integration is merged in [PR1106](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/1106) at `4927939b0776218d13e911d0472ca320af459f28`. It extends the existing Operating Plans application, its saved revisions and its receiving workflow.

The operator starts with an actual saved Support case and an explicitly selected immutable revision. The [native source capture](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4927939b0776218d13e911d0472ca320af459f28/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/oauth-operating-source.mjs) retains that revision's complete previous chain, original case metadata, workspace and runtime bodies, and the exact OAuth source files referenced by those versions. This is a separate private companion for the operating plan. Capturing it reads the selected case; it does not change the live case head or invoke the OAuth producer.

The compact plan source records the case ID and selected revision, earlier revision identities, original before/after observations, repair actions and exact artifact references. Each reference identifies a retained path, byte count and SHA-256. Missing source values and incomplete coverage stay visible. The full private case, source bodies and reports remain in the companion, while the ordinary plan carries the references needed to select and review them.

The [plan builder and result recorder](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4927939b0776218d13e911d0472ca320af459f28/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/discovery/support-operating-plan.mjs) create seven editable phases: sources, authority, observation, response, recovery, case and handover. The operator supplies the customer, owner, period and saved time and chooses actual discovered command registrations and arguments. The resulting plan gives the next operator a sequence of work and its source context. Existing applications continue to perform that work; saving a plan does not execute a command, restart a watcher or complete an incident.

After an operation returns, the operator records its human summary and selects the retained evidence IDs that support that outcome. A completed step requires at least one existing evidence ID. The recorder checks the same source case and its selected revision or retained lineage, so a later case edition can contribute its actual returned evidence without silently mixing another customer's case. Each recorded result creates an ordinary plan revision and retains earlier instructions and outcomes.

The [existing browser integration](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4927939b0776218d13e911d0472ca320af459f28/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/discovery/public/support-operating-plan.mjs) supports source import, plan preparation and evidence selection within Operating Plans. It preserves an existing unsaved browser draft before receiving the updated plan and rechecks the originally selected source and step. The [installed command](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4927939b0776218d13e911d0472ca320af459f28/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/discovery/support-operating-cli.mjs) exposes the same customer journey through `starforge support-operating-plan`: capture or receive the private source companion, create the plan, record returned work, and inspect, compare or receive its complete history.

Customer handover therefore contains two related selections. The ordinary plan is received through the existing full-history rules: matching history is reused, a later receiving head is preserved, and divergent revisions remain an explicit conflict. The private source companion is separately received into a fresh private directory and verified through the original CaseStore and runtime codecs. Its deterministic receipt binds the descriptor, complete selected case lineage, manifest and original artifact bytes. The [native receiving guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4927939b0776218d13e911d0472ca320af459f28/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/OAUTH_OPERATING_RECEIVING.md) defines those selections and same-request recovery, including adoption of a complete destination after a lost acknowledgment.

The [complete operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/4927939b0776218d13e911d0472ca320af459f28/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/discovery/OAUTH_SUPPORT_OPERATING_PLANS.md) joins these interfaces into capture, review, plan creation, returned-work recording and customer receiving. Native acceptance remains attached to the original OAuth programme and the actual case and receiving artifacts it returns. The plan's completion evidence is recorded only after those original results exist.

### Retain the producer boundary before receiving

The [original native programme](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/d49f7be36d3cf06ccb85e0eb6d6fcb410a46e02d/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf93-seller-support-bundle/oauth-native-programme.mjs) contains one integrated demonstration: real JOSE signing and verification, original MCP HTTP handling, the protected observation endpoint, controlled original dependency failure, SF93 opening/acknowledgment/recovery, and SF74 case/export/import/reopening. This programme remains with its existing execution owner; its source is not an execution receipt.

Before invoking customer receiving, the producer saves both exact final source files and a private non-secret context. The [retained receiving helper](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/d49f7be36d3cf06ccb85e0eb6d6fcb410a46e02d/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf93-seller-support-bundle/oauth-receive-context.mjs) binds that context to the original stopped watcher, selected incident revisions, captures, source implementations, Node identity and optional browser paths. It acquires the existing kernel and incident-worker leases before continuing the same receiving request.

When the original producer has ended, a retained-only continuation can consume those exact files and incident records without recreating the OAuth host, signing another token, restarting the watcher or sending another incident notification. The old host addresses remain historical input. The continuation still needs the original incident store, complete application source, writable private customer directories and its local Support listeners. Its separate receipt never relabels a failed producer as a single successful invocation.

### Installed product and grant contribution

The [selected Merchant Support recipe](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/d49f7be36d3cf06ccb85e0eb6d6fcb410a46e02d/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/selections/merchant-support.json) includes the original Support and incident components, complete OAuth browser assets and guides, the original `mcp-oauth` command, four public OAuth module exports and their declaration files. The [package operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/d49f7be36d3cf06ccb85e0eb6d6fcb410a46e02d/products/merchant-support/PACKAGE_README.md) explains the existing runtime installer and `mcp` dependency feature. Selecting a source recipe does not itself install JOSE, OpenSSL, Python or an optional browser; those are explicit original runtime prerequisites.

For a customer engagement, the existing Commercial, Implementation and Technical/customer receiving desks remain the place to agree scope, assign the work, attach the actual delivered case and record the customer's response. This capability sits within the canonical USD 38,000, 400-hour, 150-day, six-package scope. Its customer outcomes and actual commercial results continue through the existing application and customer records.

The next acceptance step is the already-owned native programme and its original returned artifacts. After that result exists, the cumulative publisher can attach its exact outcome and limits to this same chapter and source registration, then receive the existing four reviewer outputs into the original saved draft and review.

## DCAT catalogue migration, accepted editions and recurring customer delivery

The catalogue migration application gives a data publisher or implementation partner a practical way to prepare a source catalogue, explain its changes and hand the complete reviewed project to another operator. It is part of the existing merchant workspace. Its contribution to the Stellar programme is a usable data preparation and operating capability that merchants can incorporate into a useful customer service. The completed source engineering and GSA migration exercise are pre-award work. The funded programme remains the existing merchant integration, customer delivery, facilitator interoperability and launch work.

A catalogue release is the operator's decision about a particular reviewed document. Payment authorization, Stellar settlement and delivery of a purchased resource remain the responsibility of the existing merchant and facilitator components. The grant milestones join those components to an actual customer use case, with the existing useful-purchase and independent-operator criteria.

### A complete catalogue job

The [installed migration procedure](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/58ce16a5eca080b6f082d2db884ac55f34f67cc3/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/MIGRATION_OPERATING.md) follows the job from the original document to an independently receivable project. An operator receives a complete DCAT-US 1.1 or 3.0 catalogue, retains its original bytes and selects the source, optional comparison edition and any independently edited candidate. The original GSA converter and selected schemas perform conversion and validation. The review also follows catalogue members, identifier relocations, typed identity mappings and complete field changes. An already-3.0 document can be preserved byte for byte; flat-3.0 normalization is an explicit selection.

The saved review distinguishes source validation, candidate validation and conservation. It retains corrections-needed results as working material, including a conversion report that has no candidate. The operator can inspect full record values and every page of findings, download the original documents and report, correct a candidate or an identity decision, then prepare another review. Original inputs and preceding reports stay available throughout this process. Exact JSON handling preserves the source's numeric values when identifiers or field values exceed ordinary JavaScript number precision.

An accepted release selects the exact reviewed candidate and records its predecessor. Cutover binds the inspected active release and candidate/review hashes. Rollback creates a new entry selecting an earlier candidate, retaining the intervening reviews and decisions. The complete workspace archive carries documents, findings, corrections and release history to the receiving operator. The [original runtime and conversion guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/58ce16a5eca080b6f082d2db884ac55f34f67cc3/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/DCAT_ENGINE.md) describes the converter, schema selection, validation and complete report; the [installed package entrypoint](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/58ce16a5eca080b6f082d2db884ac55f34f67cc3/products/ckan/PACKAGE_README.md) connects the same project to Applications, commands and operating guides.

The browser, command line and merchant agent interfaces operate the same saved project and original workspace lease. An operator can begin with a browser review, continue through the command line or MCP tools, then export and reopen the same complete project. This makes the deliverable useful for a small publisher operating its own catalogue and for a partner who commissions an implementation and transfers responsibility to customer staff.

### What the original GSA run established

The [complete original native operation record](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/15f308030131c33573240f5d035d52e320d24c5d/operations/dcat-gsa-migration-20261012-390e/NATIVE_OPERATION.json) retains the executed migration, preservation and reviewed-correction phases. The operation used the actual complete legacy and current GSA catalogue documents, each with 344 catalogue members, the unchanged original converter and schemas, and the explicitly selected portable Python runtime. The original dependency and runtime selection is documented in [PORTABLE_RUNTIME.md](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/58ce16a5eca080b6f082d2db884ac55f34f67cc3/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/PORTABLE_RUNTIME.md).

|Executed phase|Complete source and candidate result|Operator consequence|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|Convert the legacy DCAT-US 1.1 catalogue|All 344 source members matched the candidate; zero members were added or lost. The candidate was exactly the original converter's 789,204-byte output. Eleven promoted series identifiers failed IRI validation.|The complete review retained the original candidate and identified the corrections required before receiving it.|
|Preserve the current DCAT-US 3.0 catalogue|All 344 members were retained, with no record changes or validation errors. The candidate was byte-identical to the original 756,457-byte document.|The review accepted that exact preserved document.|
|Review the explicitly corrected legacy candidate|Eleven explicit typed identity mappings resolved the series identifiers. All 344 members remained conserved, with zero additions, losses or validation errors. The corrected candidate contained 789,521 bytes.|The independent reviewed candidate became receivable while the original conversion and its findings remained available.|


The legacy conversion exposed 1,994 field changes and four catalogue-level changes. The complete review made those changes inspectable instead of reducing the migration to a count of successful records. The corrected phase retained the full mapping file and exact candidate; the 3.0 preservation phase established a separate unchanged-document outcome. These results support the technical feasibility of detecting a real migration problem, making an explicit correction and retaining enough original material for another operator to inspect the decision.

The operation retained 21 complete artifacts in a 4,429,949-byte archive. The source operation records the complete input, candidate, mapping, report and archive hashes. Those identities allow the installed customer operation to consume the already-completed domain result without repeating or reinterpreting that migration.

The whole installed customer receiving programme has been published with its complete source, original Git objects, dependency selection and domain inputs. Its installation, managed Applications, browser, CLI, MCP and independent receiving phases are queued as one original customer operation. Completion of those phases will add the actual installed-runtime and customer-interface results to the retained domain outcome. The current technical result is the executed original catalogue operation described above.

### Following editions and retained publisher history

The [recurring catalogue procedure](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/58ce16a5eca080b6f082d2db884ac55f34f67cc3/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/RECURRING_CATALOGS.md) extends the same project to a publisher's current HTTPS document. The operator saves the original publication URL, declared or automatically detected profile, private token environment reference when needed, request limits and a due-check interval. Each changed configuration becomes a retained version, and the selection history records subsequent choices between versions.

An acquisition retains the actual request and redirect history, response status, relevant cache and retry headers, exact response bytes, byte count and completeness. A bounded partial response remains inspectable as a partial response. Public conditional requests can reuse a saved edition only when its original binding and retained bytes still match. Sources using a private token reference receive complete entities, and credentials stay in the host's private environment. Publisher retry deadlines remain effective across configuration changes and redirects.

The operator then selects the latest acquired document and an explicit accepted predecessor release. The comparison binds that release's candidate and review hashes. Any accepted identity decisions to carry forward are selected individually from the predecessor's complete report. With an automatic candidate, those decisions resolve against the newly converted current source while its other fields remain fresh. With an explicitly uploaded corrected candidate, its bytes remain unchanged and the selected decisions are resolved against the current source and candidate using their typed identifiers, catalogue scope and record role. Missing, ambiguous or overlapping selections become a preparation finding requiring an explicit correction.

This produces a repeatable service: acquire a following publisher edition, inspect its source and changes, resolve the selected decisions, prepare a review and release the chosen candidate through the existing operation. Acquisition alone leaves the current accepted release intact. Failed and interrupted attempts remain in history, and an explicit retry links to the original attempt.

The installed due-check command uses the host's existing scheduler. While the application is open, it verifies the original private startup record and dispatches through the running workspace owner. When the workspace is closed, it obtains the existing lease. Busy workspaces defer to the next scheduled invocation, and both the saved interval and publisher retry deadline remain effective. This preserves one operation owner across interactive and recurring work.

Source versions, acquisition receipts and bodies, complete reviews, typed mapping decisions and release history travel in the original whole-workspace archive. The receiving operator supplies the destination's private environment, reopens the saved project and continues from the retained latest-edition identity.

### Customer installation and independent receiving

The [complete recurring customer programme](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/58ce16a5eca080b6f082d2db884ac55f34f67cc3/operations/dcat-recurring-catalog-390e-20261013/README.md) joins the original domain operation to the existing browser and archive receiver in one process. It receives the selected source, inspects the actual source and acquisition history, reads complete review pages and original files, submits a current-source review and exports the resulting whole workspace. The receiving phase uses that post-review archive and its exact hash. A separately opened application then inspects the received history and complete state.

The programme keeps the domain operation, browser operation and received-project reopening as separate results under one customer operation. Its final outcome is complete only when all three actual phases complete. The source and operating guide are shipped; the next native execution will produce the retained interface and receiving artifacts for that selected installation. The original standalone source edition remains identified, so a later application edition can be compared explicitly rather than silently replacing the programme being received.

For a customer's deployment, the implementation partner selects one actual catalogue, the destination environment, the required output and the person responsible for acceptance. The operator delivers the reviewed candidate plus the complete editable project, runs the customer's export or publication procedure, and records the selected candidate and deployment context. Subsequent editions reuse the saved operating procedure and the customer's original acceptance responsibilities.

### Commercial use and the Stellar customer outcome

A practical initial workshare is catalogue migration and operator handover for one publisher: source discovery and retention, schema and identity review, an explicitly corrected candidate when needed, one deployment/export integration and a complete receiving session. The offer names the selected catalogue, destination environment, useful output, implementation schedule and receiving criteria. Customer-specific source size, identity problems, deployment requirements and acceptance determine the scope and price. The original commercial case retains the offer, customer decisions and payment terms.

The same complete project gives a partner an ongoing edition service to sell after commissioning. The operator retains what was downloaded, why a candidate changed, which decisions were carried forward and what the customer accepted. A customer can receive the editable project and continue operating it, while the partner can provide later acquisition, review and deployment work under an explicit scope.

The Stellar programme's useful paid unit must still be selected through the original merchant offer: a particular advertised resource or service output, with its request, price, authorization, payment result and useful delivered bytes. A locally accepted catalogue may be an input to that service, or an explicitly selected deliverable, depending on the actual offer and source permissions. The funded integration makes that relationship concrete for the participating merchants and buyers, and validates it through the existing independent-facilitator and customer-use criteria.

Partner outreach and the proposed workshare provide a route to customer discovery and commissioning. The grant's adoption measures remain the original independent merchants, independent buyers and actual useful purchases. The completed GSA migration contributes engineering feasibility to that effort.

### Pre-award work and the existing funded packages

The catalogue application, the executed 344-record domain operation, source declarations, recurring acquisition workflow and complete customer programmes were prepared before an award. They are starting assets for the proposed work. The grant request remains **USD 38,000 for 400 prospective hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance**, with the existing six packages and their original owners, deliverables and acceptance conditions.

Where a participating merchant selects a catalogue-based service, these assets support the existing packages as follows.

|Existing funded package|Allocation|Catalogue contribution to the prospective customer work|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|Tranche 1: Merchant-resource integration, by day 30|80 hours / USD 7,600|Select the participating merchant's actual catalogue service or output, connect its original source and required destination, and bind the useful advertised resource to the existing merchant delivery.|
|Tranche 1: Authority and handover, by day 30|40 hours / USD 3,800|Establish the customer's source permissions, private runtime responsibilities, acceptance decisions and operating handover. Receive the actual project with the responsible operator.|
|Tranche 2: Provider and ledger deployment, by day 90|70 hours / USD 6,650|Join the selected useful catalogue-derived output to the original request, authorization, facilitator and payment records. Evaluate the same useful service through the existing two independent facilitator paths.|
|Tranche 2: Deployed threat response, by day 90|50 hours / USD 4,750|Complete the customer environment's source, credential, interrupted-operation and recovery work; retain actual failed attempts and the operator's subsequent continuation.|
|Tranche 3: Mainnet rollout, by day 150|90 hours / USD 8,550|Operate the participating merchants' selected useful offerings and customer deliveries through the existing mainnet programme, retaining actual purchase and delivery outcomes.|
|Tranche 3: Production recovery and handover, by day 150|70 hours / USD 6,650|Complete independent staff receiving, recurring-edition operation, rollback and restoration in the actual customer installations, including the original project and source history.|


These are contributions within the existing allocations. The catalogue chapter adds no separate grant tranche or retroactive development charge. By day 90, two independent buyers must complete at least ten useful testnet purchases in total during seven consecutive days ending by day 90, with both merchants represented; the same useful service must complete through two independent facilitators. By day 150, both merchants operate on mainnet and two independent buyers complete at least thirty useful purchases in total during fourteen consecutive days ending by day 150, with both merchants represented. Both buyers return on another UTC day for a distinct completed purchase. The selected catalogue service must meet those original definitions when its purchases contribute to the count.

The engineering programme can therefore begin with a source-backed working catalogue application, a completed real migration example and a portable operator procedure. The remaining funded work is the customer-specific integration and operation that turns those assets into a useful merchant service and an independently receivable customer deployment.

## Customer operating procedures and returned work

### The customer receives working instructions and a continuing record

A customer installation needs a named person to operate it after delivery: what to open, which source and reporting period to use, what to run, what result to expect, and how the next person continues. The installed Operating Plans application gives that work an editable procedure with ordered steps, responsible people, dates, progress and full recorded results. The customer keeps the complete saved history alongside the native workspace and readable handover.

A step can contain a manual task or an actual registration from the selected toolkit. A registered step retains the installed package identity, original command or provider, source records and declared runtime groups. Its exact argument array stays with the entered instructions. The operator performs the action in its original application and then records the actual outcome in the plan. This lets the handover explain both the useful result and the concrete source and operation needed to reproduce or continue it.

The original [Operating Plans guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/710507fb46d1a401026254bad259a6f4deb88f88/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/discovery/OPERATING_PLANS.md) covers the browser, complete editable JSON, printable HTML and Markdown, original catalog comparison, terminal commands and typed API. The [maintained history model](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/710507fb46d1a401026254bad259a6f4deb88f88/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/discovery/operating-plan.mjs) supplies the shared saved-revision and receiving behavior.

### Prepare customer work from the selected grant packages

The original SCF planning review can prepare the customer's procedure directly from its retained native planning file and selected revision. The user chooses the original work packages and enters the customer, operating owner, useful result and receiving destination. Each generated step carries the native package ID, remaining work, completion measure, prospective price, hours, relative day window and tranche deliverable. Optional bindings select actual installed toolkit registrations.

The preparation retains the entire source relationship: original filename and byte count, source SHA-256, native plan identity and revision, content and scenario digests, exact selected package IDs and selected totals. A complete original prepared copy stays inside the planning review. The operator receives an ordinary editable Operating Plan and can add detailed instructions, actual due dates and the original command arguments in its maintained editor.

The current six-package application remains **$38,000, 400 prospective hours and 150 days**. Its preparation uses the original selected native values for merchant resource integration, authority handover, provider and ledger deployment, deployed threat response, mainnet rollout, and production recovery and handover. Native grant, budget, payment and calendar calculations continue in the original SF47 workspace. The customer procedure records how the selected work is carried out and handed over.

The complete [grant-to-customer operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/710507fb46d1a401026254bad259a6f4deb88f88/stellar-forge/developer-site/GRANT_OPERATING_PLANS.md) and [native preparation and return model](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/710507fb46d1a401026254bad259a6f4deb88f88/stellar-forge/developer-site/dist/grant-operating-plan-core.mjs) supply that joined workflow.

### Perform, hand over and return the same procedure

The complete customer course uses the existing applications:

1. **Prepare the selected work.** Open the team's original submission and native planning review. Select its saved source revision and work packages, name the customer and operating owner, then create the operating procedure.
2. **Open the customer's working plan.** Start Command finder at the regular browser address and import the complete plan into Operating Plans. Enter the reporting period, responsible people, actual source locations, exact arguments and receiving instructions.
3. **Record the work as it occurs.** Run the selected operations in their original applications. Save the procedure's full result, progress and actual dates. Each saved revision retains the earlier instructions, registrations and results.
4. **Deliver complete working files.** Keep the full editable plan with the original native workspace and customer deliverables. Export readable HTML or Markdown from the intended saved revision for the receiving person.
5. **Review the customer's returned work.** Reopen the original grant planning review and open the complete returned Operating Plan. Compare each original package with the returned owner, due date, status, instructions and full recorded result.
6. **Review the actual sequence.** Read the complete originally prepared, previously selected and returned step lists. The comparison shows their positions and added or removed steps, and indicates when the sequence changed.
7. **Receive the current comparison.** Enter the review note and explicitly receive the later matching history. The original prepared copy remains available; the current continuing plan includes the complete received history and its receiving entry.
8. **Continue with the next operator.** Save and export the original submission with the retained customer work. Download its current plan or readable handover for the next person, using the same native case and selected customer procedure.

The [saved planning editor](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/710507fb46d1a401026254bad259a6f4deb88f88/stellar-forge/developer-site/dist/grant-operating-plan-workspace.mjs) implements the browser course. The [installed command](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/36f1786ef88267addc955473cde7420427a820ce/stellar-forge/developer-site/grant-operating-plan.mjs) performs preparation, comparison, retained-plan export and complete submission receiving through the same model. The [typed API](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/710507fb46d1a401026254bad259a6f4deb88f88/stellar-forge/developer-site/dist/grant-operating-plan-core.d.mts) carries the original source, full preparation, continuation, pending review and ordered comparison for integrating applications.

### Complete customer outputs travel with their operating steps

An operator can attach the actual report, dataset, image or other complete output to its step. The original file name, media type, byte count, full binary contents and receiving note stay in that saved revision. A corrected file receives its own identity; earlier saved revisions retain the original. The next operator can select an earlier revision and download its exact file, receive the complete editable plan, or open the standalone HTML handover with its embedded original downloads.

The [customer operating editor](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/710507fb46d1a401026254bad259a6f4deb88f88/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/discovery/public/operating-plan.mjs) selects multiple original files and retains unfinished work through the existing draft recovery. The [installed file commands](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/255f85043ba5d01eff07436b11db5e82dab8af9b/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/discovery/operating-plan-cli.mjs) attach whole files, list a selected revision, extract complete bytes to a new named destination and remove a file from a following revision. The [typed customer file interface](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/710507fb46d1a401026254bad259a6f4deb88f88/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/discovery/operating-plan.d.mts) exposes the same full-content model to receiving applications.

The original grant package comparison shows added, removed and changed files against both the prepared and previously selected procedure. Named downloads expose the complete prepared, previous and returned contents, including outputs on additional customer steps. The saved unfinished return and later matching history carry those same complete bytes into the original planning review. The ordinary plan and grant submission retain their existing whole-document capacities, including source and saved history; large original native archives continue through their maintained delivery.

### Preserve unfinished work and conflicting copies

Opening a returned file stores its complete incoming plan, filename, original planning source and native revision, entered receiving note and compared operating revision in the saved original planning selection. Save, retained versions, restored drafts and complete draft export/reopen carry that unfinished work. A reviewer can stop midway and resume with the whole file and note present. Opening, refreshing, closing or receiving retains the preceding complete draft.

If the continuing procedure advances after the return was compared, the reviewer can explicitly refresh against its current history while preserving the opened file and note. Acceptance checks the selected comparison revision. The full pending download remains accessible if the current history conflicts.

The original Operating Plans receiver compares every shared saved revision. An identical or older matching return keeps the later current history. A later matching return extends it. A divergent copy keeps its complete history through the original copy and conflict controls. A received grant procedure retains its original preparation and a single complete continuing history with ordered receiving ranges.

The command-line receiver uses the same behavior. It retains a matching saved review note when no replacement is supplied, preserves unrelated pending work, and exports actual matching replay cleanup with the preceding whole draft retained. An unchanged replay retains the current complete draft state.

### Use the same operating model for actual aid-data cases

The IATI product prepares its customer procedure from a selected saved document-evidence case. Its full package retains the original organisation plan, complete selected evidence history, every document row and observation, existing comparisons, exact correction draft and actual installed catalog. The ordinary operating plan then carries the customer's review, correction, complete export, independent receiving and following-period work.

The original IATI application remains responsible for document observations, named decisions, publisher corrections and native receiving. The procedure makes those actions and their recorded results usable by the receiving operator. The customer can edit the plan in Operating Plans, receive a later complete matching plan back into the original IATI package, and transfer it with the complete native evidence workspace.

A5F3's [complete IATI customer guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/0110a7fde307112abee5be63a06291855aa72599/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/iati/document_evidence/OPERATING_PROCEDURES.md) and [original procedure adapter](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/0110a7fde307112abee5be63a06291855aa72599/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/iati/document_evidence/operating_procedure.mjs) provide this product-specific join. Its existing native capture and receiving stay attached to the original selected IATI case.

## ROZO payment operations, financial closing and complete receiving

ROZO payment operations connects the merchant’s original provider requests, retained observations and reconciliation reports to the configured Accounting and Buyer applications. Staff can carry a selected report through recognition, source review, exact allocations, dated period closing, accountant review and complete project receiving. The original request, report edition and financial decisions remain linked when another operator takes over the installation.

This is an implemented product contribution to the existing Stellar merchant workspace. It supplies reusable customer commissioning and financial receiving software for the same prospective integrations described in the application. The current source selection includes the configured-finance release in PR1064 and the following-edition correction workflow in PR1138 at 47c67eecca93ffa3cc95731a24ef03ccba9264d9. Native installation and full customer receiving continue through the original ROZO commissioning operation; its returned completion records establish the operated edition.

### Commission the original merchant installation

The commissioning workorder selects the actual merchant, provider connection, receiving engineer, source context, retained ROZO workspace, existing merchant configuration and its Accounting/Buyer aliases. It names the person responsible for source acceptance, period decisions, accountant review, backup and receiving. The [maintained installation guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/a480c70a6cb4b5dfa89976d2978013af9b70794e/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/selections/ROZO_PAYMENTS.md) and [complete runtime selection](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/47c67eecca93ffa3cc95731a24ef03ccba9264d9/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/selections/rozo-payments.json) build the original product together with its schema and MCP dependencies. Applications reviews, saves, starts and opens that same selected installation.

The [Applications provider](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/a480c70a6cb4b5dfa89976d2978013af9b70794e/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/rozo-payments/application-provider.mjs) binds the original workspace and connection configuration, including the selected merchant configuration and any separate Buyer connection file. Host-local environment references supply provider credentials and the existing encrypted-backup passphrase. Staff use the original provider mode and declared source context throughout the operation. A received active workspace continues its own identity, requests and history.

### Operate the payment and report before its financial close

The merchant creates and tracks its original provider request, retains complete callback and polling observations, reconciles incoming payment, fee and destination evidence, and saves the selected period report. A report is selected by its identifier, version and complete original SHA-256. The source retains that report’s JSON, CSV/HTML presentation and original payment objects, so a later renderer or following observation does not replace an earlier captured edition.

The [original financial source reader](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/a480c70a6cb4b5dfa89976d2978013af9b70794e/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/rozo-payments/finance-source.mjs) preserves three independently typed movements: source payment, source fee and destination payout. Each keeps its native units, original chain/network, token address, symbol and decimal precision. Provider confirmation retains its provider provenance. An expected, absent, unsettled or unresolved amount remains visible for review. Commercial valuation, account recognition and Buyer ownership are explicit later decisions.

### Give the accountant complete work and receive the actual return

Each accountant handoff is created from its exact issued close and original source hash. Merchant and Buyer handoffs retain their distinct typed source. The [complete operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/47c67eecca93ffa3cc95731a24ef03ccba9264d9/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/rozo-payments/FINANCE.md) begins with a read-only finance plan generated from the actual saved report and configured workspaces. The resulting complete archive includes original ROZO source/evidence, all Accounting operating files in their encrypted backup, the full Buyer application/database/source project, original and returned accountant files, selected plans, original requests, native results and receiving records. The [archive receiver](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/47c67eecca93ffa3cc95731a24ef03ccba9264d9/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/rozo-payments/finance-archive.py) verifies every declared member before application execution. A later provider report can change a previously recognised movement or its supporting source. A matching request already recorded by the original financial owner replays its existing result before those fresh-state checks.

The [complete following-edition programme](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/47c67eecca93ffa3cc95731a24ef03ccba9264d9/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/rozo-payments/finance-amendment-native.mjs) starts from the selected first programme’s completed source and full archive. The [operating and receiving guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/47c67eecca93ffa3cc95731a24ef03ccba9264d9/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/rozo-payments/FINANCE_AMENDMENTS.md) gives the actual plan, native execution, interruption and receiving commands.

This reusable implementation supports the existing authority, deployed-response and production-recovery packages. ### Review catalogue changes and continue the same customer request

The [complete catalogue review and handover guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/a1ec07c422132af070399ba368587a167ad3ed23/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/partners/rialto/CATALOGUE_COMPARISON.md) extends the original offline report with a complete before/after review. The two original source texts, byte counts, hashes, source plans and coverage findings remain available alongside the review notes.

The [original comparison model](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/a1ec07c422132af070399ba368587a167ad3ed23/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/partners/rialto/comparison.mjs) compares resource URL plus tool-name identity and the complete ordered original rows. It retains the previous request draft before changing selection and preserves exact request fields in the complete handover.

The receiving customer downloads the complete comparison JSON or self-contained HTML, reopens the full sources and notes, and explicitly restores a carried draft against the matching catalogue and row. Earlier saved comparisons remain available when a review is replaced. These source and review files remain part of the same customer task and the existing funded scope.

## Stellarcarbon customer statements and continuing partner reporting

Stellarcarbon contributions can be turned into a complete customer reporting service using the delivered local statements desk. A reporting operator receives a whole original source edition, assigns actual customers and projects, inspects each contribution and certificate, saves dated statements and hands the complete editable workspace to another operator. Browser, CLI, typed client and Merchant Applications use the same saved operation. The [complete customer guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/47b9c48bda957598c67d04abc8d5cbbd7ba04933/products/stellarcarbon-statements/README.md) and [original source contract](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/47b9c48bda957598c67d04abc8d5cbbd7ba04933/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/partners/stellarcarbon-statements/README.md) describe the installed workflow.

### Complete customer operation

The staff operator selects an authorized native backup or the official API, the source network and reporting periods. The native backup retains all seven original tables. API capture follows complete transaction and retirement pages and closes related certificates and transactions. Source editions preserve whole original files, exact numeric strings, acquisition scope and available-table coverage. A later API edition can be compared with the backup without treating unacquired distribution and minted-block tables as deleted records.

Actual customer names and projects are operator assignments, separate from source funders, recipients and VCS projects. The operator can assign an individual transaction, recipient or funder, review conflicting assignments and save the current mapping. A statement freezes its original source, customer selection and assignment revision. Later corrections produce another saved version.

Every customer period includes readable HTML, complete JSON and three CSV files covering contributions, certificate allocations and the separately dated retirement register. Contribution dates select the reporting period; all certificate allocations known in the retained source edition remain associated, including later retirements. Whole certificate VCUs and a customer's attributed CARBON are separate measures. Summing every original fill preserves the actual completed amount even when an earlier allocation's native finalized flag is false.

The public April 14, 2026 backup contains 39 contributions totaling 49.158 CARBON, with 49.000 allocated. The retained October 12 API edition contains 40 contributions, 25 certificates and 44 allocations: 52.440 CARBON contributed, 52.000 allocated and 0.440 remaining. In the worked November 2025 customer statement, the original 1.177 contribution advances from 1.019 allocated to 1.177 allocated; the final 0.158 is supplied by a certificate dated July 23, 2026. The November certificate-date register remains empty. This concrete later-retirement case demonstrates why the source edition, contribution period and certificate period travel together.

Staff can export all source editions, mappings, statement versions and history, receive the complete workspace in a distinct private directory, reopen it and continue editing. Individual customer deliveries contain that customer's selected statement files; full staff receiving carries the operating workspace.

### Commissioned installation and the funded programme

The prepared commercial workshare offers one partner installation, up to ten customer mappings, two historical periods and the first current period, full exports and staff receiving for EUR 1,500, divided into EUR 750 kickoff and EUR 750 accepted delivery. Its scope is ten active business days and two review rounds. Optional EUR 150 monthly operation covers one source refresh, up to ten customer statements plus consolidation, one correction round and two staff hours. The actual source owner, scope and commercial terms enter the original Workshare and [Stellarcarbon Installation profile](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/47b9c48bda957598c67d04abc8d5cbbd7ba04933/stellar/scf_2026/sf49_data_commissioning/installation-workorders/stellarcarbon.json) through the [maintained carbon commissioning workflow](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/47b9c48bda957598c67d04abc8d5cbbd7ba04933/stellar/scf_2026/sf49_data_commissioning/installation-workorders/CARBON_REPORTING.md).

The native accounting connection selects the original Merchant customer and accepts the service fee explicitly. It creates or recovers the same invoice draft from the original request journal; the existing invoice and calendar payment-plan applications continue that case. CARBON quantities and source asset payments retain their original reporting meaning.

For a selected funded service, T1 configures the customer's authorized source, useful report unit, receiving operator and handover. T2 connects that same useful unit to the existing merchant/buyer payment flow and operates the original fulfillment/recovery conditions across the selected facilitators. T3 supplies recurring mainnet use and independent production restoration. The original six-package programme remains USD 38,000 for 400 prospective hours over 150 days; the installation records which remaining adaptations belong to that programme or the commissioned service.

### Original source and receiving

The [native receiving guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/47b9c48bda957598c67d04abc8d5cbbd7ba04933/products/carbon-native-receiving/README.md) carries both complete applications through source intake, actual browser forms and downloads, independent receiving, closed-store reopening and a whole-source archive. Its current continuation preserves completed stages and the original accounting draft. The existing native run completed both Stellarcarbon editions, November and July customer exports, original accounting preparation and independent Carbon receiving before the GiveCredit intake process exited with signal 9. The original saved operation supplies the remaining native continuation.

[Complete retained-source and two-application receiving procedure](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/47b9c48bda957598c67d04abc8d5cbbd7ba04933/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/partners/carbon-native-receiving/README.md) · [Original complete Stellarcarbon implementation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/tree/47b9c48bda957598c67d04abc8d5cbbd7ba04933/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/partners/stellarcarbon-statements)

## GiveCredit donor reporting, provider pools and carbon allocation

The delivered GiveCredit desk connects original donation records and receipt payment identities to successful Stellar transfers, pooled provider payouts and Stellarcarbon retirement allocations. Registry, ledger and carbon editions remain individually retained. Operators save the associations and funding decisions used for a donor, initiative or consolidated statement, then receive that complete editable work independently. The [customer operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/47b9c48bda957598c67d04abc8d5cbbd7ba04933/products/cfce-givecredit-statements/README.md) and [original registry and contract source](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/47b9c48bda957598c67d04abc8d5cbbd7ba04933/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/partners/cfce-givecredit-statements/README.md) define the complete workflow.

### Original donation to customer statement

A staff operator selects the actual organization, original Credits deployment, provider, source dates and reporting groups. Authorized registry capture follows every original list page and includes each donation's impact relationships. Whole original exports can enter through the same intake. Native ledger capture retains complete RPC, Horizon and historical XDR responses, exact token atoms, network and application order. The [historical ledger source operation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/47b9c48bda957598c67d04abc8d5cbbd7ba04933/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/partners/carbon-native-receiving/HISTORICAL_LEDGER_SOURCES.md) can close an existing native ledger selection, acquire a finite interval or reselect retained original pages for another observed provider.

The receipt's original payment hash anchors its source transaction; the saved assignment selects the successful transfer using its network, transaction/envelope and operation or event identity, asset and amount. Its minted-token identifier describes the separate receipt. When the legacy Donation UUID association is absent, staff save an explicit association using the original successful transfer and its source explanation. Shared payments retain explicit allocated amounts and are counted once.

The pool register distinguishes incoming donations, immediate vendor payments, provider bucket payouts, accounted provider remainder and actual token balance. Each balance carries its observation ledger. Source-dated fees and ordered events determine funding capacity; current getters do not supply historical rates. A provider and vendor can share an address, so outgoing transfers are interpreted within their original donation call or receive an explicit saved operator classification.

Staff allocate each whole provider payout using original gross-payment weights, native oldest-first order or explicit payment amounts. Original provider capacity limits those allocations, and vendor fees remain outside reusable funding. Payout-to-sink associations retain the selected funding revision and the source that connects the actual transactions. A later funding edit is adopted by an existing association through an explicit update, preserving earlier donor attribution and statement versions.

The statement selects registry creation dates or payment ledger-close dates. It delivers HTML, full JSON and seven CSV files for donations, payments, payout funding, carbon contributions, certificate allocations, the dated retirement register and original receipts. Original token values, reported registry USD, CARBON attribution and certificate VCUs remain separately identified. Donor attribution follows the saved source bridge and funding method; it is not inferred from a pooled balance.

### Operate the next period and hand over

The operator receives the next complete registry, ledger or carbon edition, compares original keyed rows, carries unchanged payment associations and reviews changed funding or carbon relationships. Saved statements preserve both current and frozen funding revisions actually used. The full staff handover contains every original source, operator decision, statement version and history. Receiving creates a separate private workspace that can reopen, continue an association and issue another reporting period.

Browser, CLI, typed core/client and the existing Merchant Applications lifecycle operate this same workspace. Historical source acquisition keeps whole background pages in the received source archive and supplies selected complete original ledger responses to the editable desk. The maintained two-application receiving operation preserves its actual original checkpoint and completed Stellarcarbon stages as the GiveCredit intake and full browser continuation proceed.

### Commissioned installation and Stellar contribution

The prepared CFCE workshare offers one organization, one mainnet GiveCredit deployment and Stellarcarbon provider, up to ten initiative/customer reporting groups, two historical periods and the first current period. EUR 3,000 covers the existing desk installation and registry/receipt/pool bridge commissioning, with 50% at kickoff and 50% on accepted delivery over ten active business days after the selected source access is available. Optional EUR 250 monthly operation covers the agreed refresh and reporting scope. The [complete CFCE Installation profile](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/47b9c48bda957598c67d04abc8d5cbbd7ba04933/stellar/scf_2026/sf49_data_commissioning/installation-workorders/cfce-givecredit.json) binds the actual source owner, reporting reviewer, commercial case and receiving operator to the maintained Grant Operations workorder.

This is a concrete application of Stellar transaction semantics to a useful recurring customer service. Original transfer identities, token scales, fee-bump aliases, successful execution, application order and source-dated Soroban pool settings determine financial attribution. The saved customer result remains editable and traceable to its original source as another engineer receives it.

For an independently selected funded installation, the existing T1 packages configure the registry/source contract and full receiving task; T2 connects the agreed report resource to native purchasing, monitoring and interrupted-delivery recovery; T3 operates recurring mainnet service and production handover. The existing six-package budget and independent-use targets govern that selection. Donation transfers, receipt NFTs, carbon retirement and purchases of the reporting service retain their own native records.

[Complete GiveCredit source](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/tree/47b9c48bda957598c67d04abc8d5cbbd7ba04933/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/partners/cfce-givecredit-statements)

## Original grant accounts and saved operating work

The grant operator can carry an original bank statement through reviewed cash, account reconciliation and complete case receiving. CSV uses explicit column, date and number mapping; OFX / QFX and MT940 retain their original account sections and parser reports. The operator reviews each movement, classification, supplier allocation and opening or closing balance before one case transaction receives the batch. Stable account and provider identities preserve distinct payments and recognize overlapping statements. Original cash corrections retain the payment history and the link back to the bank source.

The operating desk groups planning, people, accounts, customers and review work in a neutral interface. **Find in case** searches complete permitted record populations, original source metadata and saved workflow summaries. It opens the exact statement inputs, reconciliation revision, funding edition, issuer terms, cohort comparison or grant procedure in its original desk. Named staff visibility follows the current case permissions. Switching to saved work preserves open drafts and unresolved original requests, including the comparison editor's unsaved commercial fields.

Browser, native CLI, typed client and Merchant operations share the same case and saved identities. Complete account and case exports retain original source bytes, invoice allocations, correction history and selected editions for another installed workspace. The published receiving programme uses the four unchanged original input files and the maintained product to perform desktop and phone entry, request recovery, repeated statements, native bank review, account export, independent import and cold reopening. Its retained continuation records the actual case, request and receiving results as that original operation progresses.

This implemented operating capability supports the existing delivery, integration and handover scope. The canonical proposal continues to control the award request, prospective hours, milestones and customer outcome counts.

### Reopen the retained purchase

Use the maintained runtime installation with native Stellar packages, the MCP feature and operator support. Retain the selected source archive, complete lock and READY installation. In Applications choose **Grant purchase reviewer**, select that runtime and a private workbench directory, then use **Review → Save → Connect → Start → Open**. Leaving Packet and SHA-256 empty selects the bundled original purchase; an existing exported packet uses its exact digest. The installed command is:

~~~sh
starforge grant-demo workbench --dir /srv/starforge/state/grant-review --port 0
~~~

The full original guide covers private parent ownership, instance access, both retained quotes, complete results, closed Buyer export and receiving. This route reopens retained work; opening the page itself does not launch an application.
